sentences.zh: 曾怘，字仲常，中書舍人鞏之孫。

translations.literal: Zeng Ku, style name Zhongchang, was the grandson of the Secretariat Drafter Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Ku, styled Zhongchang, was a grandson of the Secretariat Drafter Gong.

sentences.zh: 補太學內舍生，以父任郊社齋郎，累官司農丞、通判溫州，須次於越。

translations.literal: He was enrolled as an Inner Student of the Imperial Academy, and through his father's privilege was appointed Suburban Sacrifice Attendant; he rose through the posts of Vice Commissioner of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and Vice Prefect of Wenzhou, and was awaiting his turn to take office in Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial Academy as an inner student and, through his father's privilege, received appointment as Suburban Sacrifice Attendant. He rose through the posts of vice commissioner of the Court of the Imperial Granaries and vice prefect of Wenzhou, and was then waiting his turn to take up office in Yue.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，金人陷越，以琶八為帥，約詰旦城中文武官並詣府，有不至及藏匿、不覺察者，皆死。

translations.literal: In the third year of the Jianyan reign, when the Jurchens captured Yue, they made Pa Ba commander and stipulated that at dawn all civil and military officials in the city were to come to the headquarters; anyone who failed to appear, or who concealed others, or who failed to detect such concealment, would be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, when the Jurchens took Yue, they placed Pa Ba in command and required every civil and military official in the city to report to headquarters at dawn the next day. Anyone who failed to appear, who hid others, or who failed to uncover such concealment was to be executed.

sentences.zh: 怘獨不往，為鄰人糾察逮捕，見琶八，辭氣不屈。

translations.literal: Ku alone did not go; a neighbor reported and seized him, and when he was brought before Pa Ba his words and bearing did not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Ku alone refused to go. A neighbor reported him and he was arrested. Brought before Pa Ba, he spoke and stood his ground without yielding.

sentences.zh: 且言：“國家何負汝，乃叛盟欺天，恣為不道。

translations.literal: He also said, "What has the state done to wrong you, that you should break the treaty, deceive Heaven, and wantonly commit outrage?
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "What has the Song done to you, that you should break your treaty, defy Heaven, and commit such outrages at will?

sentences.zh: 我宋世臣也，恨無尺寸柄以死國，安能貪生事爾狗奴邪？

translations.literal: I am a hereditary minister of Song; I regret that I have not even a hand's breadth of authority with which to die for the state—how could I cling to life and serve you dog-slaves?"
translations.idiomatic: I am a hereditary minister of Song. I only regret that I lack even the smallest authority with which to die for my country. How could I cling to life and serve you dog-slaves?"

sentences.zh: ”時金人帳中執兵者皆愕眙相視，琶八曰：“且令出。

translations.literal: " At that time all the armed men in the Jurchen camp stared at one another in astonishment. Pa Ba said, "For now let him out.
translations.idiomatic: " The armed men in the Jurchen camp all stared at one another in astonishment. Pa Ba said, "For now, let him go.

sentences.zh: ”左右盡驅其家屬四十口同日殺之越南門外，越人作窖瘞其屍。

translations.literal: " His attendants then drove out all forty members of his household and killed them on the same day outside the southern gate of Yue; the people of Yue dug pits and buried the bodies.
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants then rounded up all forty members of his household and killed them the same day outside Yue's southern gate. The people of Yue dug pits and buried the bodies.

sentences.zh: 金人去，怘弟朝散郎懸時知杭州餘杭縣事，製大棺斂其骨，葬之天柱山。

translations.literal: After the Jurchens withdrew, Ku's younger brother Xuan, a Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement, was serving as magistrate of Yuhang County in Hang Prefecture; he had a large coffin made to gather the bones and buried them on Mount Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens withdrew, Ku's younger brother Xuan, a Gentleman for Meritorious Achievement then serving as magistrate of Yuhang in Hang Prefecture, had a large coffin made to gather the bones and buried them on Mount Tianzhu.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予三資恩澤，官其弟怤、子崈、兄子 {宀居}，皆將仕郎。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was granted three grades of favor; his younger brother Fu, his son Cui, and his elder brother's son Ju were all given office as Gentlemen in Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported to the throne, the court granted three grades of favor. His younger brother Fu, his son Cui, and his elder brother's son Ju were all given office as Gentlemen in Attendance.

sentences.zh: 方遇難時，崇甫四歲，與乳母張皆死。

translations.literal: At the time of the calamity, Chongfu was four years old; he and his wet nurse Zhang were both reported dead.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of the massacre, Chongfu was four years old; he and his wet nurse Zhang were both reported dead.

sentences.zh: 夜值小雨，張得蘇，顧見崇亦蘇，尚吮其乳，郡卒陳海匿崇以歸。

translations.literal: That night a light rain fell; Zhang revived, and looking back saw that Chong had also revived and was still suckling at her breast. A district soldier named Chen Hai hid Chong and brought him home.
translations.idiomatic: That night a light rain fell. Zhang revived, and when she looked back she saw that Chong had revived as well and was still nursing at her breast. A district soldier named Chen Hai hid Chong and brought him home.

sentences.zh: 後仕至知南安軍。

translations.literal: He later rose in office to Prefect of Nan'an Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose in office to become prefect of Nan'an Circuit.

sentences.zh: 怘從弟悟。

translations.literal: Ku's younger cousin was Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Ku's younger cousin was Wu.

sentences.zh: 悟字蒙伯，翰林學士肇之孫也。

translations.literal: Wu, style name Mengbo, was the grandson of the Hanlin Academician Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wu, styled Mengbo, was a grandson of the Hanlin Academician Zhao.

sentences.zh: 宣和二年進士，靖康間為亳州士曹。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of the Xuanhe reign; during the Jingkang period he served as a clerical officer in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination in the second year of Xuanhe and, during the Jingkang crisis, served as a clerical officer in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 金人破亳州，悟被執，抗辭慢罵，眾刃劘之，屍體無存者，妻孥同日被害。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens took Bozhou, Wu was seized; he spoke defiantly and reviled them, and many blades hacked him to pieces until no body remained; his wife and children were killed on the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens took Bozhou, Wu was seized. He spoke defiantly and reviled them until many blades hacked him apart and no body remained. His wife and children were killed the same day.

sentences.zh: 年三十三。

translations.literal: He was thirty-three years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-three.

sentences.zh: 劉汲，字直夫，眉州丹棱人。

translations.literal: Liu Ji, style name Zhifu, was a native of Danling in Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, styled Zhifu, was a native of Danling in Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 紹聖四年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the fourth year of the Shaosheng reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination in the fourth year of Shaosheng.

sentences.zh: 為合州司理、武信軍推官，改宣德郎、知開封府鄢陵縣。

translations.literal: He served as judicial officer of Hezhou and investigating censor of the Wuxin Army, then was promoted to Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and appointed magistrate of Yanling County in Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judicial officer of Hezhou and investigating censor of the Wuxin Army, then was promoted to Gentleman for Promoting Virtue and appointed magistrate of Yanling in Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奉行神霄宮不如令，以京畿轉運使趙霆奏，徙通判隆德府。

translations.literal: Because he did not carry out the orders regarding the Divine Empyrean Palace as required, the Capital Region transport commissioner Zhao Ting memorialized against him, and he was transferred to vice prefect of Longde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Because he failed to carry out the orders regarding the Divine Empyrean Palace as required, the capital-region transport commissioner Zhao Ting memorialized against him and he was transferred to vice prefect of Longde Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時方士林靈素用事，郡人班自改《易係辭》為妖言，以應靈素。

translations.literal: At that time the Daoist master Lin Lingsu was in power; a man of the prefecture named Ban Zi altered the "Appended Remarks" of the Book of Changes into heterodox speech to accord with Lingsu.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Daoist master Lin Lingsu held sway at court. A man of the prefecture named Ban Zi altered the "Appended Remarks" of the Book of Changes into heterodox speech to suit Lingsu.

sentences.zh: 汲攝守，下自獄。

translations.literal: Ji, acting as prefect, had Zi imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Ji, serving as acting prefect, had Zi imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 靈素薦自有道。

translations.literal: Lingsu recommended that Zi possessed the Way.
translations.idiomatic: Lingsu recommended Zi as a man who possessed the Way.

sentences.zh: 命轉運使陳知存按驗，掾史懼，欲變獄。

translations.literal: He ordered the transport commissioner Chen Zhicun to investigate and verify the case; the clerks were afraid and wished to alter the outcome of the trial.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered transport commissioner Chen Zhicun to investigate. The clerks were afraid and wanted to alter the outcome of the case.

sentences.zh: 汲責數掾史，知存憚之，卒以實聞。

translations.literal: Ji rebuked the clerks repeatedly; Zhicun feared him and in the end reported the facts as they were.
translations.idiomatic: Ji rebuked the clerks sharply. Zhicun feared him and in the end reported the facts as they stood.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯京師，諸道不知朝廷動息者三月。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens again attacked the capital, the various circuits had no word of the court's movements for three months.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens again attacked the capital, the circuits went three months without word of the court's movements.

sentences.zh: 馮延緒傳詔撫諭，謂車駕出郊定和議，令諸道罷兵。

translations.literal: Feng Yanxu transmitted an edict of reassurance, saying that the imperial carriage had gone out of the city to settle a peace agreement and ordering the circuits to halt their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yanxu transmitted an edict of reassurance, saying that the emperor had gone out of the city to settle a peace agreement and ordering the circuits to halt their armies.

sentences.zh: 汲謂副總管高公純曰：“詔書未可遽信。

translations.literal: Ji said to the deputy commander Gao Gongchun, "The edict must not be believed hastily.
translations.idiomatic: Ji said to the deputy commander Gao Gongchun, "This edict must not be believed too quickly.

sentences.zh: ”公純問故，汲曰：“詔下以去年十二月，鄧去京七百里，今始至州何也？

translations.literal: " Gongchun asked why. Ji said, "The edict was issued last December, and Deng is seven hundred li from the capital—how is it only now reaching the prefecture?
translations.idiomatic: " Gongchun asked why. Ji said, "The edict was issued last December. Deng is seven hundred li from the capital—how has it only now reached us?

sentences.zh: 安有議和以三月，而敵猶未退乎？

translations.literal: How can there have been peace talks for three months while the enemy still has not withdrawn?
translations.idiomatic: How can there have been peace talks for three months while the enemy still has not withdrawn?

sentences.zh: 此必金人脅朝廷以款勤王之師爾，可速進兵。

translations.literal: This must be the Jurchens coercing the court to mollify the armies coming to rescue the throne. Advance the troops quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens must be coercing the court into placating the armies coming to rescue the throne. Advance at once.

sentences.zh: ”公純難之，汲請自行，公純不得已俱至南陽，不進，汲獨馳數十騎赴都城，二帝已北行，汲素服慟哭。

translations.literal: " Gongchun found this difficult. Ji asked to go himself; Gongchun had no choice but to go with him to Nanyang, yet they did not advance. Ji alone galloped with several dozen horsemen to the capital; the two emperors had already gone north. Ji put on plain mourning dress and wept in anguish.
translations.idiomatic: " Gongchun hesitated. Ji asked to go himself, and Gongchun had no choice but to accompany him to Nanyang, yet they still did not advance. Ji alone galloped with several dozen horsemen to the capital. The two emperors had already been taken north. He put on plain mourning dress and wept in anguish.

sentences.zh: 尋代公純攝帥事，捐金帛饗士，為戰守計。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he replaced Gongchun as acting commander, contributed gold and silk to feast the troops, and made plans for fighting and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he replaced Gongchun as acting commander, contributed gold and silk to feast the troops, and laid plans for fighting and defense.

sentences.zh: 詔鄧州備巡幸，汲廣城池，飾行闕，所以待乘輿之具甚備。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Dengzhou to prepare for an imperial tour; Ji enlarged the city walls, adorned the traveling palace, and made every provision for receiving the imperial carriage extremely complete.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Dengzhou to prepare for an imperial tour. Ji enlarged the city walls, adorned the traveling palace, and made every provision for receiving the imperial carriage with exceptional thoroughness.

sentences.zh: 就加直龍圖閣、知鄧州兼京西路安撫使。

translations.literal: He was thereupon promoted to Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall, appointed prefect of Dengzhou, and concurrently made Pacification Commissioner of the Jingxi West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon promoted to Direct Associate of the Dragon Diagram Hall, appointed prefect of Dengzhou, and concurrently made Pacification Commissioner of the Jingxi West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 汲奏：“欲復兩河，當先河東，欲復河東，當用陝兵，請先從事河東，以定西河之根本。

translations.literal: Ji memorialized, "To recover the Two He regions, one must first take Hedong; to recover Hedong, one must use Shaanxi troops. I ask to begin with Hedong first, in order to secure the foundation of the western He region.
translations.idiomatic: Ji memorialized, "To recover the Two He regions, one must first take Hedong; to recover Hedong, one must use Shaanxi troops. I ask to begin with Hedong first, in order to secure the foundation of the western He region.

sentences.zh: ”於是金人復渡河，諜知鄧州為行在所，命其將銀朱急攻京西。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the Jurchens again crossed the river; spies learned that Dengzhou was the traveling court, and they ordered their general Yin Zhu to press the attack on Jingxi West.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon the Jurchens crossed the river again. Spies learned that Dengzhou was serving as the traveling court, and they ordered their general Yin Zhu to press the attack on Jingxi West.

sentences.zh: 汲遣副總管侯成林守南陽，金人奄至，殺成林。

translations.literal: Ji sent the deputy commander Hou Chenglin to hold Nanyang; the Jurchens arrived suddenly and killed Chenglin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji sent the deputy commander Hou Chenglin to hold Nanyang. The Jurchens arrived suddenly and killed Chenglin.

sentences.zh: 汲集將吏謂曰：“吾受國恩，恨未得死所，金人來必死，汝有能與吾俱死者乎？

translations.literal: Ji gathered the generals and officials and said, "I have received the state's grace and regret that I have not yet found a place to die. When the Jurchens come I shall certainly die. Are there any among you able to die with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji gathered the generals and officials and said, "I have received the state's grace and regret that I have not yet found a place to die. When the Jurchens come I shall certainly die. Is there anyone among you able to die with me?"

sentences.zh: ”皆流涕曰：“惟命。

translations.literal: " All wept and said, "We await your command.
translations.idiomatic: " All wept and said, "We await your command.

sentences.zh: ”民有請涉山作砦以避敵者，汲曰：“是棄城矣。

translations.literal: " Some of the people asked to cross the mountains and build stockades to avoid the enemy. Ji said, "That would be abandoning the city.
translations.idiomatic: " Some civilians asked to cross the mountains and build stockades to avoid the enemy. Ji said, "That would mean abandoning the city.

sentences.zh: 然若屬俱死無益。

translations.literal: Yet if all of you die together it will serve no purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if all of you die together it will serve no purpose.

sentences.zh: ”乃下令曰：“城中有材武願從軍者聽留，餘從便。

translations.literal: " He then issued an order: "Within the city, those with martial talent who wish to join the army may remain; the rest may do as they please.
translations.idiomatic: " He then issued an order: "Anyone in the city with martial talent who wishes to join the army may remain; the rest may do as they please.

sentences.zh: ”得敢死士四百人。

translations.literal: " He obtained four hundred dare-to-die troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He obtained four hundred dare-to-die troops.

sentences.zh: 又令曰：“凡仕於此，其聽送其家，寅出午反，違者從軍法。

translations.literal: He issued another order: "All who hold office here may send for their families; they are to leave at the yin hour and return by the wu hour. Violators will be dealt with under military law.
translations.idiomatic: He issued another order: "All who hold office here may send for their families. They are to leave at dawn and return by noon. Violators will be dealt with under military law.

sentences.zh: ”眾皆感服，無一人失期。

translations.literal: " All were moved and submitted; not one person missed the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: " All were moved and submitted. Not one person missed the deadline.

sentences.zh: 及南陽陷，命將戚鼎將兵三千逆戰，及命靳儀與趙宗印分西、南門犄之。

translations.literal: When Nanyang fell, he ordered the general Qi Ding to lead three thousand troops to meet the enemy in battle, and ordered Jin Yi and Zhao Zongyin to hold the western and southern gates in mutual support.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanyang fell, he ordered the general Qi Ding to lead three thousand troops to meet the enemy in battle, and ordered Jin Yi and Zhao Zongyin to hold the western and southern gates in mutual support.

sentences.zh: 汲自以牙兵四百登陴望，見宗印從間道遁，即自至鼎軍中，麾其眾陣以待，敵至皆死鬥，敵卻。

translations.literal: Ji himself took four hundred personal guards and climbed the wall to look out; seeing Zongyin flee by a hidden path, he went at once to Ding's army, deployed the troops in formation to await the enemy, and when the enemy arrived they all fought to the death until the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Ji himself took four hundred personal guards and climbed the wall to look out. Seeing Zongyin flee by a hidden path, he went at once to Ding's army, deployed the troops in formation to await the enemy, and when the enemy arrived they all fought to the death until the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄而儀敗，金人攻之益急，矢下如雨，軍中請汲去，汲不許，曰：“使敵知安撫使在此為國家致死。

translations.literal: Soon Yi was defeated; the Jurchens pressed the attack ever harder, arrows falling like rain. The army asked Ji to withdraw, but he would not permit it and said, "Let the enemy know that the Pacification Commissioner is here, dying for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yi was defeated. The Jurchens pressed the attack ever harder, arrows falling like rain. The army asked Ji to withdraw, but he refused and said, "Let the enemy know that the Pacification Commissioner is here, dying for the state.

sentences.zh: ”敵大至，汲死之。

translations.literal: " The enemy came in force and Ji died.
translations.idiomatic: " The enemy came in force and Ji died.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈太中大夫，諡忠介。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported to the throne, he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and given the posthumous title Loyal and Upright.

sentences.zh: 鄭驤，字潛翁，信之玉山人。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiang, style name Qianweng, was a native of Yushan in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiang, styled Qianweng, was a native of Yushan in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 登元符三年進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination in the third year of the Yuanfu reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination in the third year of Yuanfu.

sentences.zh: 知溧陽縣，歲饑，民多逃亡。

translations.literal: As magistrate of Liyang County, in a year of famine many of the people fled.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Liyang County, in a year of famine many of the people fled.

sentences.zh: 漕司按籍督逋賦不少貸，驤患之，盡去其籍。

translations.literal: The transport office checked the registers and pressed collection of arrears without granting relief; Xiang was troubled by this and removed all the registers entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The transport office checked the registers and pressed collection of tax arrears without granting relief. Xiang was troubled by this and destroyed all the registers.

sentences.zh: 使者欲繩以法，驤曰：“著令約二稅為定數，今不除，則逋愈多，民愈貧，賦愈不辦。

translations.literal: The envoy wished to punish him by law. Xiang said, "The established regulations fix the two taxes as a set amount; if they are not now remitted, arrears will only grow greater, the people will grow poorer, and the taxes will become ever harder to collect.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy wished to punish him by law. Xiang said, "The established regulations fix the two taxes as a set amount. If they are not remitted now, arrears will only grow, the people will grow poorer, and the taxes will become ever harder to collect.

sentences.zh: ”使者不能屈。

translations.literal: " The envoy could not make him yield.
translations.idiomatic: " The envoy could not make him yield.

sentences.zh: 時議自建康鑿漕渠導太湖以通大江，將破數州民田，調江、浙二十五州丁夫，所費百萬計。

translations.literal: At the time it was proposed to cut a transport canal from Jiankang to channel Lake Tai into the Great River, which would ruin farmland across several prefectures and require corvée labor from twenty-five prefectures in Jiang and Zhe, at a cost reckoned in the millions.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was proposed to cut a transport canal from Jiankang to channel Lake Tai into the Yangtze, which would ruin farmland across several prefectures and require corvée labor from twenty-five prefectures in Jiang and Zhe at a cost reckoned in the millions.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣官視可否，驤條析利病，力止之。

translations.literal: The court sent officials to inspect whether the project was feasible; Xiang itemized its benefits and harms and strenuously stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent officials to inspect whether the project was feasible. Xiang itemized its benefits and harms and strenuously stopped it.

sentences.zh: 通判岢嵐軍，改慶陽府。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of the Ke Lan Army and was transferred to Qingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of the Ke Lan Army and was transferred to Qingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 姚古奏為熙河蘭廓路經略司屬官。

translations.literal: Yao Gu memorialized to appoint him as a staff officer of the Xianhe Lan Kuo Circuit Pacification Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Gu memorialized to appoint him as a staff officer of the Xianhe Lan Kuo Circuit Pacification Commission.

sentences.zh: 錢蓋自渭易熙，奏辟幕下。

translations.literal: When Qian Gai was transferred from Wei to Xi, he memorialized to recruit Xiang onto his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Gai was transferred from Wei to Xi, he memorialized to recruit Xiang onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 地震，秦隴金城六城壞，驤為蓋言六城熙河重地，宜趣繕治，因自請董兵護築益機灘新堡六百步，以控西夏。

translations.literal: An earthquake damaged the six cities of Jincheng in Qin-Long; Xiang told Gai that the Six Cities were a vital region of Xianhe and should be repaired at once, and thereupon asked on his own initiative to lead troops in supervising the construction of a new fort six hundred paces long at Yiji Beach to control the Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: An earthquake damaged the six cities of Jincheng in Qin-Long. Xiang told Gai that the Six Cities were a vital region of Xianhe and should be repaired at once, and thereupon asked on his own initiative to lead troops in supervising the construction of a new fort six hundred paces long at Yiji Beach to control the Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 堡成，以功遷官，賜緋衣銀魚。

translations.literal: When the fort was completed, he was promoted in office for his merit and granted crimson robes and a silver fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: When the fort was completed, he was promoted for his merit and granted crimson robes and a silver fish tally.

sentences.zh: 唃廝羅氏舊據青唐，置西寧州，董氈入朝，其弟益麻黨征走西夏。

translations.literal: The Gusiluo clan had formerly held Qingtang and established Xining Prefecture; Dong Zhan came to court, while his younger brother Yima Dangzheng fled to the Western Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The Gusiluo clan had formerly held Qingtang and established Xining Prefecture. Dong Zhan came to court, while his younger brother Yima Dangzheng fled to the Western Xia.

sentences.zh: 大觀中，羌人假其名歸附，童貫奏賜姓名趙懷恭，官團練使。

translations.literal: During the Daguan period, Qiang tribesmen used his name to submit in allegiance; Tong Guan memorialized to grant him the surname Zhao and the personal name Huaigong, with the office of regimental training commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daguan period, Qiang tribesmen used his name to submit in allegiance. Tong Guan memorialized to grant him the surname Zhao and the personal name Huaigong, with the office of regimental training commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至是黨征自西寧求歸，貫懼事露，議者希貫意欲絕之。

translations.literal: At this time Dangzheng came from Xining seeking to return; Guan feared the affair would be exposed, and those in council, hoping to please Guan's intent, wished to cut him off.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Dangzheng came from Xining seeking to return. Guan feared the affair would be exposed, and those in council, hoping to please Guan's intent, wished to cut him off.

sentences.zh: 驤謂貫欺君，請辨其偽。

translations.literal: Xiang said that Guan was deceiving the sovereign and asked to distinguish the impostor.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said that Guan was deceiving the sovereign and asked to distinguish the impostor.

sentences.zh: 貫怒，將厚誣以罪，會敗而止。

translations.literal: Guan was enraged and was about to frame him with a heavy charge, but the affair collapsed and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guan was enraged and was about to frame him with a heavy charge, but the affair collapsed and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 擢京兆府等路提舉常平。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries for the Jingzhao Prefecture and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries for the Jingzhao Prefecture and other circuits.

sentences.zh: 驤按格為《常平總目》十卷，頒之所部。

translations.literal: Xiang compiled according to regulations the General Catalogue of the Ever-Normal System in ten scrolls and promulgated it within his jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang compiled according to regulations the General Catalogue of the Ever-Normal System in ten scrolls and promulgated it within his jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 時陝右大稔，驤奏乞以所部本息乘時廣糴，得米六十萬斛。

translations.literal: At that time Shaanxi West had a great harvest; Xiang memorialized asking to use the principal and interest under his jurisdiction to buy grain widely while prices were favorable, obtaining six hundred thousand hu of rice.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Shaanxi West had a great harvest. Xiang memorialized asking to use the principal and interest under his jurisdiction to buy grain widely while prices were favorable, obtaining six hundred thousand hu of rice.

sentences.zh: 高宗初，以直秘閣知同州兼沿河安撫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, he was made Direct Associate of the Secretariat Pavilion, appointed prefect of Tongzhou, and concurrently made Pacification Commissioner Along the River.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Gaozong's reign, he was made Direct Associate of the Secretariat Pavilion, appointed prefect of Tongzhou, and concurrently made Pacification Commissioner Along the River.

sentences.zh: 時謀巡近甸金陵、南陽、長安為駐蹕計，驤言：“南陽、金陵偏方，非興王地；

translations.literal: At the time they were planning an imperial tour of the nearby districts, considering Jinling, Nanyang, and Chang'an as places for the court to halt; Xiang said, "Nanyang and Jinling are partial regions, not places where dynasties rise;
translations.idiomatic: At the time they were planning an imperial tour of the nearby districts, considering Jinling, Nanyang, and Chang'an as places for the court to halt. Xiang said, "Nanyang and Jinling are partial regions, not places where dynasties rise;

sentences.zh: 長安四塞，天府之國，可以駐蹕。

translations.literal: Chang'an is enclosed on four sides and is a land of the heavenly treasury—it can serve for the court to halt."
translations.idiomatic: Chang'an is enclosed on four sides and is a land of the heavenly treasury. It can serve for the court to halt."

sentences.zh: ”會帝東幸揚州，復請自楚、泗、汴、洛以迄陝、華，各募精兵，首尾相應，庶敵勢不得衝決。

translations.literal: " When the emperor went east to Yangzhou, he again requested that from Chu, Si, Bian, and Luo through to Shaan and Hua, each place recruit elite troops so that head and tail could respond to one another, in the hope that the enemy's force could not break through.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor went east to Yangzhou, he again requested that from Chu, Si, Bian, and Luo through to Shaan and Hua, each place recruit elite troops so that head and tail could respond to one another, in the hope that the enemy's force could not break through.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: He received no response.
translations.idiomatic: He received no response.

sentences.zh: 金將婁宿犯同州及韓城，驤遣兵拒險擊之，師失利，金人乘勝徑至城下，通判以下皆遁去。

translations.literal: The Jurchen general Lou Su attacked Tongzhou and Hancheng; Xiang sent troops to hold the defiles and strike them, but the army was defeated. The Jurchens pressed their advantage straight to the city walls, and from the vice prefect downward all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen general Lou Su attacked Tongzhou and Hancheng. Xiang sent troops to hold the defiles and strike them, but the army was defeated. The Jurchens pressed their advantage straight to the city walls, and from the vice prefect downward all fled.

sentences.zh: 驤曰：“所謂太守者，守死而已。

translations.literal: Xiang said, "What is called a prefect is one who holds the city and dies—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang said, "What is called a prefect is one who holds the city and dies—that is all.

sentences.zh: ”翼日城陷，驤赴井死，贈通議大夫、樞密直學士，諡威湣，詔賜廟湣節。

translations.literal: " The next day the city fell; Xiang threw himself into a well and died. He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Court Discussion and Academician Expositor-in-ordinary of the Privy Council, given the posthumous title Majestic and Lamented, and an edict granted him a temple with the title Lamented Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: " The next day the city fell. Xiang threw himself into a well and died. He was posthumously granted Grand Master of Court Discussion and Academician Expositor-in-ordinary of the Privy Council, given the posthumous title Majestic and Lamented, and an edict granted him a temple with the title Lamented Integrity.

sentences.zh: 驤在熙河，嚐摭熙寧迄政和攻取建置之跡為《拓邊錄》十卷，兵將蕃漢雜事為《別錄》八十卷，圖畫西蕃、西夏、回鶻、盧甘諸國人物圖書為《河隴人物志》十卷，序讚普迄溪巴溫、董氈世族為《蕃譜係》十卷。

translations.literal: While Xiang was in Xianhe, he once compiled the record of campaigns and establishments from the Xining through the Zhenghe reigns into the Records of Frontier Expansion in ten scrolls; military affairs and mixed matters of Tangut, Han, and other peoples into the Separate Records in eighty scrolls; illustrated figures and writings of the Western Tangut, Western Xia, Uyghur, Lugan, and other states into the Biographical Records of the He-Long Region in ten scrolls; and arranged and praised the Gusiluo, Xiba, and Dong Zhan clans into the Genealogies of the Barbarian Peoples in ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: While Xiang was in Xianhe, he compiled the record of campaigns and establishments from the Xining through the Zhenghe reigns into the Records of Frontier Expansion in ten scrolls; military affairs and mixed matters of Tangut, Han, and other peoples into the Separate Records in eighty scrolls; illustrated figures and writings of the Western Tangut, Western Xia, Uyghur, Lugan, and other states into the Biographical Records of the He-Long Region in ten scrolls; and arranged and praised the Gusiluo, Xiba, and Dong Zhan clans into the Genealogies of the Barbarian Peoples in ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 呂由誠，字子明，御史中丞誨之季子。

translations.literal: Lü Youcheng, style name Ziming, was the youngest son of the Censor-in-chief Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Youcheng, styled Ziming, was the youngest son of the Censor-in-chief Hui.

sentences.zh: 幼明爽有智略，範鎮、司馬光，父友也，皆器重之。

translations.literal: From youth he was bright and clear-minded and possessed strategic ability; Fan Zhen and Sima Guang, his father's friends, all valued him highly.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was bright and clear-minded and possessed strategic ability. Fan Zhen and Sima Guang, his father's friends, all valued him highly.

sentences.zh: 以父恩補官，調鄧州酒稅，臨事精敏，老吏不能欺。

translations.literal: Through his father's privilege he received office and was assigned to the wine tax post in Dengzhou; in handling affairs he was sharp and keen, and veteran clerks could not deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's privilege he received office and was assigned to the wine tax post in Dengzhou. In handling affairs he was sharp and keen, and veteran clerks could not deceive him.

sentences.zh: 會營兵竊發，聚眾閉城，守貳逃匿，由誠親往招諭，賊斂兵聽命。

translations.literal: When camp soldiers mutinied in secret, gathered a crowd, and shut the city gates, the prefect and vice prefect fled and hid; Youcheng went in person to summon and reassure them, and the rebels laid down their arms and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When camp soldiers mutinied in secret, gathered a crowd, and shut the city gates, the prefect and vice prefect fled and hid. Youcheng went in person to summon and reassure them, and the rebels laid down their arms and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 以功遷秩，尋擢提舉三門、白波輦運，言者謂其資淺，罷之。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted in rank, and soon afterward was elevated to Intendant of the Three Gates and Baibo Imperial Transport; critics said his qualifications were shallow, and he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted in rank and soon afterward was elevated to Intendant of the Three Gates and Baibo Imperial Transport. Critics said his qualifications were shallow, and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 知合水縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Heshui County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Heshui County.

sentences.zh: 王中立、種諤征靈州，由誠部運隨軍，天寒食盡，他邑役夫多潰去，唯由誠所部分無失者。

translations.literal: When Wang Zhongli and Zhong E campaigned against Lingzhou, Youcheng supervised transport and followed the army; the weather was bitterly cold and food was exhausted, and corvée laborers from other districts mostly scattered and fled, but none under Youcheng's section were lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Zhongli and Zhong E campaigned against Lingzhou, Youcheng supervised transport and followed the army. The weather was bitterly cold and food was exhausted. Corvée laborers from other districts mostly scattered and fled, but none under Youcheng's section were lost.

sentences.zh: 尋改知乘氏縣。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was transferred to magistrate of Chengshi County.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to magistrate of Chengshi County.

sentences.zh: 丞相呂大防為山陵使，辟為屬。

translations.literal: When the Chief Councillor Lü Dafang served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum, he recruited Youcheng as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief councillor Lü Dafang served as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum, he recruited Youcheng as a staff member.

sentences.zh: 通判成都府，知雅、嘉、溫、綿四州，復知嘉州，皆有治績。

translations.literal: He served as vice prefect of Chengdu Prefecture and as prefect of Ya, Jia, Wen, and Mian—four prefectures—and again as prefect of Jia; in each post he had achievements in governance.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice prefect of Chengdu Prefecture and as prefect of Ya, Jia, Wen, and Mian, and again as prefect of Jia. In each post he had achievements in governance.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，宰相唐恪薦由誠剛正有家法，宜任台臣。

translations.literal: In the first year of the Jingkang reign, the Chief Councillor Tang Que recommended Youcheng as upright and strict with family discipline, fit to serve as a censorial official.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang, the chief councillor Tang Que recommended Youcheng as upright and strict with family discipline, fit to serve as a censorial official.

sentences.zh: 召至京師，與恪議不合，且憂其蓄縮不足以濟時艱，力辭求退。

translations.literal: He was summoned to the capital, but his views did not agree with Que's, and Que also feared that his timidity would be insufficient to meet the hardships of the time; Youcheng strenuously declined and asked to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital, but his views did not agree with Que's, and Que also feared that his timidity would be insufficient to meet the hardships of the time. Youcheng strenuously declined and asked to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 差知襲慶府，未及出關，金人再入，陷京師，立張邦昌，以兵脅士大夫臣之，由誠微服得免。

translations.literal: He was assigned to prefect of Xiqing Prefecture; before he could leave the pass, the Jurchens entered again, took the capital, enthroned Zhang Bangchang, and with troops coerced the scholar-officials into serving them; Youcheng, in plain dress, escaped.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to prefect of Xiqing Prefecture. Before he could leave the pass, the Jurchens entered again, took the capital, enthroned Zhang Bangchang, and with troops coerced the scholar-officials into serving them. Youcheng, in plain dress, escaped.

sentences.zh: 時群盜所在蜂起，由誠崎嶇至郡。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were rising everywhere like bees from a hive; Youcheng made his way over rugged terrain to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At that time bandits were rising everywhere. Youcheng made his way over rugged terrain to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 城圮糧竭，於是晝夜為備，版築甫就，劇賊李昱擁十萬眾奔至城中，知其有備，陽受元帥府招安而去。

translations.literal: The walls were ruined and grain exhausted; he therefore made preparations day and night. When the ramparts had just been completed, the fierce bandit Li Yu led a hundred thousand men in a rush to the city; seeing that it was prepared, he pretended to accept amnesty from the Marshal's headquarters and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The walls were ruined and grain exhausted, so he made preparations day and night. When the ramparts had just been completed, the fierce bandit Li Yu led a hundred thousand men in a rush to the city. Seeing that it was prepared, he pretended to accept amnesty from the Marshal's headquarters and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 康王移軍濟陽，由誠竭力饋餉，軍以不乏。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Kang moved his army to Jiyang, Youcheng exerted himself to supply provisions, and the army never lacked.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang moved his army to Jiyang, Youcheng exerted himself to supply provisions, and the army never lacked.

sentences.zh: 遣官屬王允恭奉表勸進。

translations.literal: He sent his staff member Wang Yonggong to present a memorial urging the prince to ascend the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his staff member Wang Yonggong to present a memorial urging the prince to ascend the throne.

sentences.zh: 時京東諸郡，兵驕多內訌，獨由誠拊循有方，士樂為用。

translations.literal: At that time in the prefectures of Jingdong East, the troops were arrogant and prone to internal strife; Youcheng alone soothed and guided them effectively, and the soldiers were glad to serve.
translations.idiomatic: At that time in the prefectures of Jingdong East, the troops were arrogant and prone to internal strife. Youcheng alone soothed and guided them effectively, and the soldiers were glad to serve.

sentences.zh: 前後數被攻圍，屹然自立群盜中，救援皆絕。

translations.literal: He was besieged several times before and after, yet stood firm amid the bandits while all relief was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: He was besieged several times, yet stood firm amid the bandits while all relief was cut off.

sentences.zh: 孔彥舟以鄆兵叛，首犯郡境，攻之累旬不能下，始引去。

translations.literal: Kong Yanzhou rebelled with the Yan troops and was the first to invade the prefectural border; he attacked for many weeks without taking the city, and only then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yanzhou rebelled with the Yan troops and was the first to invade the prefectural border. He attacked for many weeks without taking the city and only then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 胡選者眾尤殘暴，攻由誠示必取，由誠夜焚其攻具，直入帳下，賊駭散，不知所為，忽解圍去。

translations.literal: Hu Xuan's band was especially brutal; attacking Youcheng, they showed they would certainly take the city. Youcheng burned their siege equipment by night, went straight into their camp, and the rebels scattered in terror, not knowing what to do, then suddenly lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Xuan's band was especially brutal and attacked Youcheng as if certain to take the city. Youcheng burned their siege equipment by night, went straight into their camp, and the rebels scattered in terror. Not knowing what to do, they suddenly lifted the siege and left.

sentences.zh: 一日金兵四集，由誠嚴立賞罰，厲以忠義，守兵爭奮，晝夜警備。

translations.literal: One day Jurchen troops gathered on all sides; Youcheng strictly established rewards and punishments, exhorted them with loyalty and righteousness, and the defenders vied to exert themselves, keeping watch day and night.
translations.idiomatic: One day Jurchen troops gathered on all sides. Youcheng strictly established rewards and punishments, exhorted them with loyalty and righteousness, and the defenders vied to exert themselves, keeping watch day and night.

sentences.zh: 金人百道攻城，矢石如雨，人無叛誌。

translations.literal: The Jurchens attacked the city from a hundred directions; arrows and stones fell like rain, yet no one harbored thoughts of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens attacked the city from a hundred directions. Arrows and stones fell like rain, yet no one harbored thoughts of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 郡官有迎降者，執而械之。

translations.literal: When a prefectural official wished to welcome surrender, he seized and shackled him.
translations.idiomatic: When a prefectural official wished to welcome surrender, he seized and shackled him.

sentences.zh: 判官趙令佳同心誓守，城陷俱被執。

translations.literal: The judicial administrator Zhao Lingjia shared his resolve to hold the city to the death; when the city fell they were both seized.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial administrator Zhao Lingjia shared his resolve to hold the city to the death. When the city fell they were both seized.

sentences.zh: 金人欲生降之，由誠不屈，乃殺其子仍於前，由誠不顧，與令佳同遇害。

translations.literal: The Jurchens wished to take them alive and make them submit; Youcheng would not yield, so they killed his son before his eyes, yet Youcheng paid no heed and was killed together with Lingjia.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens wished to take them alive and make them submit. Youcheng would not yield, so they killed his son before his eyes, yet Youcheng paid no heed and was killed together with Lingjia.

sentences.zh: 子偰與其家四十口皆被執，無生還者。

translations.literal: His son Yi and all forty members of his household were seized; none returned alive.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi and all forty members of his household were seized. None returned alive.

sentences.zh: 南北隔絕，其孫紹清留蜀，後自蜀走江、浙訪由誠生死，遇令佳之子子彝於江陰，知令佳與由誠同死被褒典，乃訴於朝，詔贈由誠三官，為通奉大夫，與二子恩澤。

translations.literal: North and south were cut off from one another; his grandson Shaoqing remained in Shu, and later traveled from Shu through Jiang and Zhe to learn whether Youcheng was alive or dead. He met Lingjia's son Ziyi at Jiangyin and learned that Lingjia and Youcheng had died together and been honored posthumously; he then appealed to the court, and an edict posthumously granted Youcheng three ranks as Grand Master of Court Submission and bestowed favor on two sons.
translations.idiomatic: North and south were cut off from one another. His grandson Shaoqing remained in Shu and later traveled from Shu through Jiang and Zhe to learn whether Youcheng was alive or dead. He met Lingjia's son Ziyi at Jiangyin and learned that Lingjia and Youcheng had died together and been honored posthumously. He then appealed to the court, and an edict posthumously granted Youcheng three ranks as Grand Master of Court Submission and bestowed favor on two sons.

sentences.zh: 郭永，大名府元城人。

translations.literal: Guo Yong was a native of Yuncheng in Daming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yong was a native of Yuncheng in Daming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少剛明勇決，身長七尺，須髯若神。

translations.literal: From youth he was firm, clear-minded, brave, and decisive; he stood seven feet tall, and his beard and whiskers were like those of a god.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was firm, clear-minded, brave, and decisive. He stood seven feet tall, and his beard and whiskers were like those of a god.

sentences.zh: 以祖任為丹州司法參軍，守武人，為奸利無所忌，永數引法裁之。

translations.literal: Through his grandfather's privilege he was appointed judicial aide of Danzhou; the prefect was a military man who pursued illicit profit without restraint, and Yong repeatedly invoked the law to restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Through his grandfather's privilege he was appointed judicial aide of Danzhou. The prefect was a military man who pursued illicit profit without restraint, and Yong repeatedly invoked the law to restrain him.

sentences.zh: 守大怒，盛威臨永，永不為動，則繆為好言薦之朝。

translations.literal: The prefect was greatly enraged and displayed his full authority over Yong, but Yong was unmoved; the prefect then falsely spoke well of him and recommended him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect was greatly enraged and displayed his full authority over Yong, but Yong was unmoved. The prefect then falsely spoke well of him and recommended him to the court.

sentences.zh: 後守欲變具獄，永力爭不能得，袖舉牒還之，拂衣去。

translations.literal: Later the prefect wished to alter a completed case; Yong strove against it but could not prevail, tucked the memorial under his sleeve and returned it, brushed his robe, and left.
translations.idiomatic: Later the prefect wished to alter a completed case. Yong strove against it but could not prevail, tucked the memorial under his sleeve and returned it, brushed his robe, and left.

sentences.zh: 調清河丞，尋知大穀縣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to aide of Qinghe and soon afterward appointed magistrate of Dagu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to aide of Qinghe and soon afterward appointed magistrate of Dagu County.

sentences.zh: 太原帥率用重臣，每宴饗費千金，取諸縣以給，斂諸大穀者尤亟。

translations.literal: The commander of Taiyuan habitually used high ministers; each feast cost a thousand in gold, drawn from the counties to supply it, and collections from Dagu were especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The commander of Taiyuan habitually used high ministers. Each feast cost a thousand in gold, drawn from the counties to supply it, and collections from Dagu were especially urgent.

sentences.zh: 永以書抵幕府曰：“非什一而取，皆民膏血也，以資觴豆之費可乎？

translations.literal: Yong sent a letter to the headquarters saying, "To take more than one part in ten is all the people's lifeblood—can this be used to pay for cups and dishes?
translations.idiomatic: Yong sent a letter to the headquarters saying, "To take more than one part in ten is all the people's lifeblood. Can this be used to pay for cups and dishes?

sentences.zh: 脫不獲命，令有投劾而歸耳。

translations.literal: If I cannot obtain approval, I shall submit a memorial of impeachment and return home."
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot obtain approval, I shall submit a memorial of impeachment and return home."

sentences.zh: ”府不敢迫。

translations.literal: " The headquarters did not dare press him.
translations.idiomatic: " The headquarters did not dare press him.

sentences.zh: 縣有潭出雲雨，歲旱，巫乘此嘩民，永杖巫，暴日中，雨立至，縣人刻石紀其異。

translations.literal: The county had a pool from which clouds and rain issued; in a year of drought the shamans used this to stir up the people. Yong beat the shamans and exposed them in the midday sun; rain came at once, and the people of the county carved stone to record the marvel.
translations.idiomatic: The county had a pool from which clouds and rain issued. In a year of drought the shamans used this to stir up the people. Yong beat the shamans and exposed them in the midday sun. Rain came at once, and the people of the county carved stone to record the marvel.

sentences.zh: 府遣卒數輩號“警盜”，刺諸縣短長，遊蠹不歸，莫敢迕，永械致之府，府為並它縣追還。

translations.literal: The prefecture sent several soldiers called "bandit scouts" to probe the faults of the counties; they wandered as pests and did not return, and none dared oppose them. Yong shackled them and sent them to the prefecture, which then had the other counties pursue and return them as well.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture sent several soldiers called "bandit scouts" to probe the faults of the counties. They wandered as pests and did not return, and none dared oppose them. Yong shackled them and sent them to the prefecture, which then had the other counties pursue and return them as well.

sentences.zh: 於是部使者及郡文移有不便於民者，必條利病反復，或遂寢而不行。

translations.literal: Thereafter, whenever the circuit envoy or the prefecture sent documents disadvantageous to the people, he would itemize benefits and harms in reply, and sometimes the measures were halted and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever the circuit envoy or the prefecture sent documents disadvantageous to the people, he would itemize benefits and harms in reply, and sometimes the measures were halted and not carried out.

sentences.zh: 或謂永：“世方雷同，毋以此賈禍。

translations.literal: Someone said to Yong, "The age demands conformity—do not buy disaster with this.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said to Yong, "The age demands conformity. Do not buy disaster with this.

sentences.zh: ”永曰：“吾知行吾誌而已，遑恤其它。

translations.literal: " Yong said, "I know only to follow my resolve; why should I care for anything else?
translations.idiomatic: " Yong said, "I know only to follow my resolve. Why should I care for anything else?

sentences.zh: ”大穀人安其政，以為自有令無永比者。

translations.literal: " The people of Dagu were secure under his governance and believed that since the county had had magistrates, none could compare with Yong.
translations.idiomatic: " The people of Dagu were secure under his governance and believed that since the county had had magistrates, none could compare with Yong.

sentences.zh: 既去數年，復過之，則老稚遮留如永始去。

translations.literal: Several years after he had left, when he passed through again, old and young blocked his way and detained him as when he had first departed.
translations.idiomatic: Several years after he had left, when he passed through again, old and young blocked his way and detained him as when he had first departed.

sentences.zh: 調東平府司錄參軍，府事無大小，永鹹決之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Recorder of Dongping Prefecture; matters of the prefecture, great or small, Yong decided them all.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Recorder of Dongping Prefecture. Matters of the prefecture, great or small, Yong decided them all.

sentences.zh: 吏有不能辦者，私相靳曰：“爾非郭司錄耶！

translations.literal: When clerks could not handle something, they would say to one another in private, "Are you not Recorder Guo!
translations.idiomatic: When clerks could not handle something, they would say to one another in private, "Are you not Recorder Guo!

sentences.zh: ”通判鄭州，燕山兵起，以永為其路轉運判官。

translations.literal: " He served as vice prefect of Zhengzhou; when the Yan Mountains troops rose, he was made transport vice commissioner of that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " He served as vice prefect of Zhengzhou. When the Yan Mountains troops rose, he was made transport vice commissioner of that circuit.

sentences.zh: 郭藥師屯邊，怙恩暴甚，與民市不償其直，復驅之，至壞目折支乃已。

translations.literal: Guo Yaoshi was stationed on the frontier and, relying on favor, was extremely brutal; trading with the people he would not pay fair price, and would drive them on until eyes were ruined and limbs broken before he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yaoshi was stationed on the frontier and, relying on favor, was extremely brutal. Trading with the people he would not pay fair price and would drive them on until eyes were ruined and limbs broken before he stopped.

sentences.zh: 安撫使王安中莫敢問。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong did not dare question him.
translations.idiomatic: The Pacification Commissioner Wang Anzhong did not dare question him.

sentences.zh: 永白安中，不治且難製，請見而顯責之；

translations.literal: Yong told Anzhong that if he were not disciplined it would be hard to control him, and asked to see him and openly rebuke him;
translations.idiomatic: Yong told Anzhong that if he were not disciplined it would be hard to control him and asked to see him and openly rebuke him.

sentences.zh: 不從，則取其尤者磔之市。

translations.literal: if he did not agree, then take the worst offenders and expose their corpses in the market.
translations.idiomatic: If he did not agree, then take the worst offenders and expose their corpses in the market.

sentences.zh: 乃見藥師曰：“朝廷負將軍乎？

translations.literal: He then went to see Yaoshi and said, "Has the court wronged the general?
translations.idiomatic: He then went to see Yaoshi and said, "Has the court wronged the general?

sentences.zh: ”藥師驚曰：“何謂也？

translations.literal: " Yaoshi said in alarm, "What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: " Yaoshi said in alarm, "What do you mean?

sentences.zh: ”永曰：“前日將軍杖策歸朝廷，上推赤心置將軍腹中，客遇之禮無所不至，而將軍未有尺寸功報上也。

translations.literal: " Yong said, "The other day the general came to court leaning on his staff; the emperor opened his red heart and placed the general in his bosom, treating him with every courtesy due a guest, yet the general has not repaid the court with even the smallest merit.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong said, "The other day the general came to court leaning on his staff. The emperor opened his red heart and placed the general in his bosom, treating him with every courtesy due a guest, yet the general has not repaid the court with even the smallest merit.

sentences.zh: 今乃倚將軍為重，乃縱部曲戕民不禁，平居尚爾，如緩急何！

translations.literal: Now you rely on the general's weight and let your subordinates harm the people without restraint; if this is so in ordinary times, what of emergencies!
translations.idiomatic: Now you rely on the general's weight and let your subordinates harm the people without restraint. If this is so in ordinary times, what of emergencies!

sentences.zh: ”藥師雖謝無愧容，永謂安中曰：“它日亂邊者必此人也。

translations.literal: " Although Yaoshi apologized, he showed no shame; Yong said to Anzhong, "The one who will one day bring disorder to the frontier will surely be this man.
translations.idiomatic: " Although Yaoshi apologized, he showed no shame. Yong said to Anzhong, "The one who will one day bring disorder to the frontier will surely be this man.

sentences.zh: ”已而安中罷，永亦辭去，移河北西路提舉常平。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward Anzhong was dismissed, Yong also resigned, and was transferred to Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries for Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward Anzhong was dismissed, Yong also resigned, and was transferred to Intendant of the Ever-Normal Granaries for Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 會金人趨京師，所過城邑欲立取之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens pressed toward the capital, every city and town they passed they wished to take at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens pressed toward the capital, every city and town they passed they wished to take at once.

sentences.zh: 是時天寒，城池皆凍，金率藉冰梯城，不攻而入。

translations.literal: At that time the weather was cold and the moats were frozen; the Jurchens generally used the ice as ladders to scale the walls and entered without assault.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the weather was cold and the moats were frozen. The Jurchens generally used the ice as ladders to scale the walls and entered without assault.

sentences.zh: 永適在大名，聞之，先弛壕漁之禁，人爭出漁，冰不能合。

translations.literal: Yong happened to be in Daming; when he heard of this, he first relaxed the prohibition on fishing in the moat, and people rushed out to fish so that the ice could not freeze solid.
translations.idiomatic: Yong happened to be in Daming. When he heard of this, he first relaxed the prohibition on fishing in the moat, and people rushed out to fish so that the ice could not freeze solid.

sentences.zh: 金人至城下，睥睨久之而去。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens came below the walls, they gazed up for a long time and then departed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens came below the walls, they gazed up for a long time and then departed.

sentences.zh: 遷河東提點刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Judicial Intendant of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Judicial Intendant of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 時高宗在揚州，命宗澤守京師，澤厲兵積粟，將復兩河，以大名當衝要，檄永與帥杜充、漕張益謙相掎角。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozong was in Yangzhou; he ordered Zong Ze to defend the capital. Ze trained troops and stored grain, intending to recover the Two He regions; since Daming stood at a vital point, he issued orders for Yong, the commander Du Chong, and the transport officer Zhang Yiqian to support one another.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Gaozong was in Yangzhou and ordered Zong Ze to defend the capital. Ze trained troops and stored grain, intending to recover the Two He regions. Since Daming stood at a vital point, he issued orders for Yong, the commander Du Chong, and the transport officer Zhang Yiqian to support one another.

sentences.zh: 永即朝夕謀戰守具，因結東平權邦彥為援，不數日聲振河朔，已沒州縣皆復應官軍，金人亦畏之不敢動。

translations.literal: Yong at once planned day and night for equipment of war and defense, and secured Quan Bangyan of Dongping as aid; within a few days his fame shook the north of the Yellow River, lost prefectures and counties all responded again to the government army, and the Jurchens also feared him and did not dare move.
translations.idiomatic: Yong at once planned day and night for equipment of war and defense and secured Quan Bangyan of Dongping as aid. Within a few days his fame shook the north of the Yellow River, lost prefectures and counties all responded again to the government army, and the Jurchens also feared him and did not dare move.

sentences.zh: 居亡何，澤卒，充守京師，以張益謙代之，而裴億為轉運使。

translations.literal: Before long Ze died; Chong defended the capital, Zhang Yiqian replaced him in Daming, and Pei Yi became transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Ze died. Chong defended the capital, Zhang Yiqian replaced him in Daming, and Pei Yi became transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 益謙、億齷齪小人。

translations.literal: Yiqian and Yi were base, petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqian and Yi were base, petty men.

sentences.zh: 會範瓊脅邦彥南去，劉豫舉濟南來寇，大名孤城無援，永率士晝夜乘城，伺間則出兵狙擊。

translations.literal: When Fan Qiong coerced Bangyan to go south, Liu Yu raised Jinan to invade; Daming was an isolated city without aid. Yong led the troops day and night onto the walls, and when opportunity offered sent troops out to strike in ambush.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Qiong coerced Bangyan to go south, Liu Yu raised Jinan to invade. Daming was an isolated city without aid. Yong led the troops day and night onto the walls, and when opportunity offered sent troops out to strike in ambush.

sentences.zh: 或勸益謙委城遁，永曰：“北門所以蔽遮梁、宋，彼得誌則席卷而南，朝廷危矣。

translations.literal: Someone urged Yiqian to abandon the city and flee. Yong said, "The northern gate exists to shield Liang and Song; if they achieve their aim they will sweep south, and the court will be in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Yiqian to abandon the city and flee. Yong said, "The northern gate exists to shield Liang and Song. If they achieve their aim they will sweep south, and the court will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 借力不敵，猶當死守，徐銼其鋒，待外援之至，奈何棄之？

translations.literal: Even if our strength cannot match theirs, we should still hold fast to the death, blunt their edge over time, and wait for outside aid to arrive—how can we abandon it?
translations.idiomatic: Even if our strength cannot match theirs, we should still hold fast to the death, blunt their edge over time, and wait for outside aid to arrive. How can we abandon it?

sentences.zh: ”因募士齎帛書夜縋城出，告急朝廷，乞先為備。

translations.literal: " He therefore recruited men to carry silken letters, let down by rope from the wall at night, to report the emergency to the court and beg that preparations be made in advance.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore recruited men to carry silken letters, let down by rope from the wall at night, to report the emergency to the court and beg that preparations be made in advance.

sentences.zh: 攻圍益急，俘東平、濟南人，大呼城下曰：“二郡已降。

translations.literal: The siege grew ever tighter; they captured men from Dongping and Jinan and shouted below the walls, "The two prefectures have surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: The siege grew ever tighter. They captured men from Dongping and Jinan and shouted below the walls, "The two prefectures have surrendered.

sentences.zh: 降者富貴，不降者無噍類。

translations.literal: Those who submit will be rich and honored; those who do not will leave no mouth to feed.
translations.idiomatic: Those who submit will be rich and honored; those who do not will be destroyed to the last mouth.

sentences.zh: ”益謙輩相顧色動，永大言曰：“今日正吾儕報國之時。

translations.literal: " Yiqian and the others looked at one another, their faces changing; Yong said in a loud voice, "Today is exactly the time for us to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Yiqian and the others looked at one another, their faces changing. Yong said in a loud voice, "Today is exactly the time for us to repay the state.

sentences.zh: ”又行城撫將士曰：“王師至矣，吾城堅完可守，汝曹努力，敵不足畏也。

translations.literal: " He then walked the walls comforting the officers and soldiers: "The imperial army has arrived; our walls are strong and complete and can be held. You must exert yourselves—the enemy is not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: " He then walked the walls comforting the officers and soldiers: "The imperial army has arrived. Our walls are strong and complete and can be held. You must exert yourselves—the enemy is not to be feared.

sentences.zh: ”眾感泣。

translations.literal: " The crowd was moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd was moved to tears.

sentences.zh: 質明，大霧四塞，豫以車發斷碑殘礎攻城，樓櫓皆壞，左右蒙盾而立，多碎首者。

translations.literal: At dawn, thick fog closed in on all sides; Yu used carts to hurl broken steles and ruined foundations against the city, destroying the towers and parapets; those on either side stood behind shields, and many had their heads shattered.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, thick fog closed in on all sides. Yu used carts to hurl broken steles and ruined foundations against the city, destroying the towers and parapets. Those on either side stood behind shields, and many had their heads shattered.

sentences.zh: 良久城陷，永坐城樓上，或掖之以歸，諸子環泣請去，永曰：“吾世受國恩，當以死報，然巢傾卵覆，汝輩亦何之？

translations.literal: After a long while the city fell. Yong sat on the gate tower; some tried to lead him away. His sons surrounded him weeping and begged him to leave. Yong said, "Our family has received the state's grace for generations and should repay it with death. Yet when the nest tips the eggs are crushed—where can you go?
translations.idiomatic: After a long while the city fell. Yong sat on the gate tower while some tried to lead him away. His sons surrounded him weeping and begged him to leave. Yong said, "Our family has received the state's grace for generations and should repay it with death. Yet when the nest tips the eggs are crushed—where can you go?

sentences.zh: 茲命也，奚懼。”

translations.literal: This is fate—what is there to fear?
translations.idiomatic: This is fate—what is there to fear?

sentences.zh: 益謙、億率眾迎降，金人曰：“城破始降，何也？

translations.literal: Yiqian and Yi led the crowd to welcome surrender. The Jurchens said, "You submit only after the city has fallen—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yiqian and Yi led the crowd to welcome surrender. The Jurchens said, "You submit only after the city has fallen—why?

sentences.zh: ”眾以永不從為辭。

translations.literal: " The crowd answered that Yong had refused to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd answered that Yong had refused to follow them.

sentences.zh: 金人遣騎召永，永正衣冠南向再拜訖，易幅巾而入，黏罕曰：“沮降者誰？

translations.literal: The Jurchens sent horsemen to summon Yong. Yong straightened his robes and cap, bowed twice toward the south, then changed to a plain headcloth and entered. Nianhan said, "Who obstructed the surrender?
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens sent horsemen to summon Yong. Yong straightened his robes and cap, bowed twice toward the south, then changed to a plain headcloth and entered. Nianhan said, "Who obstructed the surrender?

sentences.zh: ”永熟視曰：“ 不降者我。

translations.literal: " Yong looked at him steadily and said, "The one who would not submit is I.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong looked at him steadily and said, "The one who would not submit is I.

sentences.zh: ”金人奇永狀貌，且素聞其賢，乃自相語，欲以富貴啖永，永瞋目唾曰：“無知犬豕，恨不醢爾以報國家，何說降乎？

translations.literal: " The Jurchens marveled at Yong's appearance and had long heard of his worth; they spoke among themselves, wishing to entice him with wealth and honor. Yong glared and spat, saying, "Ignorant dogs and swine—I regret that I cannot mince you to repay the state. Why speak of surrender?
translations.idiomatic: " The Jurchens marveled at Yong's appearance and had long heard of his worth. They spoke among themselves, wishing to entice him with wealth and honor. Yong glared and spat, saying, "Ignorant dogs and swine—I regret that I cannot mince you to repay the state. Why speak of surrender?

sentences.zh: ”怒罵不絕。

translations.literal: " He raged and reviled without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " He raged and reviled without cease.

sentences.zh: 金人諱其言，麾之使去，永復厲聲曰：“胡不速殺我死？

translations.literal: The Jurchens shrank from his words and waved him away. Yong again said in a stern voice, "Why do you not quickly kill me?
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens shrank from his words and waved him away. Yong again said in a stern voice, "Why do you not quickly kill me?

sentences.zh: 當率義鬼滅爾曹。

translations.literal: I shall lead righteous ghosts to destroy you all.
translations.idiomatic: I shall lead righteous ghosts to destroy you all.

sentences.zh: ”大名人在係者無不以手加額，為之出涕，金人怒斷所舉手。

translations.literal: " The people of Daming who were bound all placed their hands on their foreheads and wept for him; the Jurchens in anger cut off the hands they had raised.
translations.idiomatic: " The people of Daming who were bound all placed their hands on their foreheads and wept for him. The Jurchens in anger cut off the hands they had raised.

sentences.zh: 乃殺之，一家皆遇害。

translations.literal: They then killed him, and his whole household was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: They then killed him, and his whole household was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 雖素不與永合者皆麵慟，金人去，相與負其屍瘞之。

translations.literal: Even those who had never agreed with Yong were moved to grief on their faces; after the Jurchens left, they together carried his corpse and buried it.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who had never agreed with Yong were moved to grief. After the Jurchens left, they together carried his corpse and buried it.

sentences.zh: 永博通古今，得錢即買書，家藏書萬卷，為文不求人知。

translations.literal: Yong was broadly learned in past and present; whenever he obtained money he bought books, and his household collection held ten thousand scrolls. In writing he sought no one's notice.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was broadly learned in past and present. Whenever he obtained money he bought books, and his household collection held ten thousand scrolls. In writing he sought no one's notice.

sentences.zh: 見古人立名節者，未嚐不慨然掩卷終日，而尤慕顏真卿為人。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw ancients who established name and integrity, he never failed to close the book in emotion for a whole day, and he especially admired Yan Zhenqing as a man.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw ancients who established name and integrity, he never failed to close the book in emotion for a whole day, and he especially admired Yan Zhenqing as a man.

sentences.zh: 充之守大名，名稱甚盛，永嚐畫數策見之，它日問其目。

translations.literal: When Chong defended Daming his reputation was very great; Yong once drafted several plans and presented them to him. Another day Chong asked what they contained.
translations.idiomatic: When Chong defended Daming his reputation was very great. Yong once drafted several plans and presented them to him. Another day Chong asked what they contained.

sentences.zh: 曰：“未暇讀也。

translations.literal: He said, "I have not yet had leisure to read them.
translations.idiomatic: He said, "I have not yet had leisure to read them.

sentences.zh: ”永數之曰：“人有誌而無才，好名而遺實，驕蹇自用而得名聲，以此當大任，鮮不顛沛者，公等足與為治乎？

translations.literal: " Yong rebuked him, saying, "A man may have resolve but lack talent, love reputation but abandon substance, be arrogant and self-willed yet gain a famous name—with such men bearing great responsibility, few escape ruin. Are you gentlemen fit to govern?
translations.idiomatic: " Yong rebuked him, saying, "A man may have resolve but lack talent, love reputation but abandon substance, be arrogant and self-willed yet gain a famous name. With such men bearing great responsibility, few escape ruin. Are you gentlemen fit to govern?

sentences.zh: ”充大慚。

translations.literal: " Chong was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Chong was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年冬，金人再犯京師，中外阻絕，或以兩宮北狩告永者，永號絕仆地，家人舁歸，不食者數日，聞大元帥府檄書至，始勉強一餐。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Jingkang, when the Jurchens again attacked the capital and inside and outside were cut off, someone told Yong that the two palaces had gone north on tour; Yong cried out and fell senseless to the ground. His family carried him home and he ate nothing for several days; only when he heard that a dispatch had arrived from the Grand Marshal's headquarters did he force himself to take one meal.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Jingkang, when the Jurchens again attacked the capital and inside and outside were cut off, someone told Yong that the two palaces had gone north on tour. Yong cried out and fell senseless to the ground. His family carried him home and he ate nothing for several days. Only when he heard that a dispatch had arrived from the Grand Marshal's headquarters did he force himself to take one meal.

sentences.zh: 其忠義蓋天性然。

translations.literal: His loyalty and righteousness were surely inborn.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty and righteousness were surely inborn.

sentences.zh: 紹興初，贈中大夫、資政殿學士，諡勇節，官其族數人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shaoxing reign he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, given the posthumous title Valiant Integrity, and several of his clan were given office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaoxing he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Palace Attendance and Academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance, given the posthumous title Valiant Integrity, and several of his clan were given office.

sentences.zh: 韓浩，丞相琦孫。

translations.literal: Han Hao was the grandson of the Chief Councillor Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hao was the grandson of the chief councillor Qi.

sentences.zh: 以奉直大夫守濰州。

translations.literal: As Grand Master for Direct Remonstrance he defended Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: As Grand Master for Direct Remonstrance he defended Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 建炎二年，金人攻城，浩率眾死守，城陷力戰死。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Jianyan reign, when the Jurchens attacked the city, Hao led the crowd in a desperate defense; when the city fell he fought to the death.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyan, when the Jurchens attacked the city, Hao led the crowd in a desperate defense. When the city fell he fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 通判朱庭傑身被數箭，亦死。

translations.literal: Vice Prefect Zhu Tingjie, his body struck by several arrows, also died.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Prefect Zhu Tingjie was struck by several arrows and also died.

sentences.zh: 權北海縣丞王允功、司理參軍王薦皆全家陷沒。

translations.literal: Acting Beihai County Assistant Magistrate Wang Yungong and Judicial Administrator Wang Jian—both their entire families were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Beihai County Assistant Magistrate Wang Yungong and Judicial Administrator Wang Jian both lost their entire families.

sentences.zh: 浩特贈三官，官其家三人。

translations.literal: Hao was specially posthumously granted three ranks, and three members of his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was posthumously granted three ranks of elevation, and three members of his family were given office.

sentences.zh: 庭傑、允功、薦各官其家一人。

translations.literal: For Tingjie, Yungong, and Jian, one member of each family was given office.
translations.idiomatic: For Tingjie, Yungong, and Jian, one member of each family was given office.

sentences.zh: 朝議大夫周中世居濰州，率家人乘城拒守，中弟辛家最富，盡散其財以享戰士。

translations.literal: Court Gentleman for Discussion Zhou Zhong had long lived in Weizhou. He led his family onto the walls to resist. Zhong's younger brother Xin's family was the wealthiest and dispersed all their wealth to feast the warriors.
translations.idiomatic: Court Gentleman for Discussion Zhou Zhong had long lived in Weizhou. He led his family onto the walls to resist the siege. Zhong's younger brother Xin's family was the wealthiest in the area and spent their entire fortune to feast the warriors.

sentences.zh: 城陷，中闔門百口皆死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Zhong's entire household of a hundred mouths all died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Zhong's entire household of a hundred souls perished.

sentences.zh: 紹興六年，以周聿請，贈官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shaoxing, at Zhou Yu's petition, he was posthumously granted office.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Shaoxing, at Zhou Yu's petition, he was posthumously granted office.

sentences.zh: 歐陽珣字全美，吉州廬陵人。

translations.literal: Ouyang Xun, styled Quanmei, was a native of Luling in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun, styled Quanmei, was a native of Luling in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 崇寧五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chongning he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongning he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調忠州學教授、南安軍司錄，知鹽官縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed Professor at the Zhongzhou school, Records Officer of Nan'an Command, and magistrate of Yanguan County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed professor at the Zhongzhou school, records officer of Nan'an Command, and magistrate of Yanguan County.

sentences.zh: 以薦上京師，遇國難，及出使，加將作監丞。

translations.literal: Recommended and sent to the capital, he encountered the national crisis; upon his mission assignment he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended and sent to the capital, he arrived amid the national crisis. When he was dispatched on a mission, he was promoted to Assistant Director of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 金人犯京師，朝議割河北絳、磁、深三鎮地講和。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens invaded the capital, the court debated ceding the three prefectures of Jiang, Ci, and Shen in Hebei to negotiate peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens invaded the capital, the court debated ceding the three Hebei prefectures of Jiang, Ci, and Shen to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 珣率其友九人上書，極言祖宗之地尺寸不可以與人。

translations.literal: Xun led nine of his friends in submitting a memorial, vehemently declaring that not even an inch of the ancestral land could be ceded to others.
translations.idiomatic: Xun led nine of his friends in submitting a memorial, declaring in the strongest terms that not even an inch of the land bequeathed by the ancestors could be given away.

sentences.zh: 及事急，會群臣議，珣復抗論當與力戰，戰敗而失其地，它日取之直；

translations.literal: When matters grew urgent and the ministers assembled to deliberate, Xun again argued forcefully that they ought to fight with all their strength: if they fought and lost the land, recovering it another day would be justified;
translations.idiomatic: When matters grew urgent and the ministers assembled to deliberate, Xun again argued forcefully that they ought to fight with all their strength. If they fought and lost the land, recovering it another day would be justified;

sentences.zh: 不戰而割其地，它日取之曲。

translations.literal: if they ceded land without fighting, recovering it another day would be unjust.
translations.idiomatic: if they ceded land without fighting, recovering it another day would be unjust.

sentences.zh: 時宰怒，欲殺珣，乃遣珣奉使割深州，珣至深州城下，慟哭謂城上人曰：“朝廷為奸臣所誤至此，吾已辦一死來矣，汝等宜勉為忠義報國。

translations.literal: The chief minister was enraged and wanted to kill Xun, so he dispatched Xun on a mission to cede Shenzhou. When Xun reached the foot of Shenzhou's walls, he wept bitterly and said to those on the walls: "The court has been misled by treacherous ministers to this pass. I have come prepared to die. You should strive in loyalty and righteousness to serve the state.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister was enraged and wanted to kill Xun, so he dispatched him on a mission to cede Shenzhou. When Xun reached the foot of the city walls, he wept bitterly and called up to the defenders: "The court has been misled by treacherous ministers to this pass. I have come prepared to die. You must strive in loyalty and righteousness to serve the state.

sentences.zh: ”金人怒，執送燕，焚死之。

translations.literal: " The Jurchens were enraged, seized him, sent him to Yan, and burned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jurchens were enraged, seized him, sent him to Yan, and burned him to death.

sentences.zh: 張忠輔，宣和末為將，同崔中、折可與守崞縣。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhongfu was a general at the end of the Xuanhe reign; together with Cui Zhong and Zhe Keyu he defended Guo County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhongfu was a general in the late Xuanhe period. Together with Cui Zhong and Zhe Keyu he defended Guo County.

sentences.zh: 金人來攻，嬰城固守，率士卒以死拒敵。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens came to attack, they enclosed the city and held firm, leading the soldiers to resist the enemy unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens came to attack, they sealed the city and held firm, leading their soldiers to resist the enemy unto death.

sentences.zh: 中度不可支，有二心。

translations.literal: Zhong judged they could not hold out and harbored second thoughts.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong judged that they could not hold out and began to waver.

sentences.zh: 忠輔宣言於眾曰：“必欲降，請先殺我。

translations.literal: Zhongfu proclaimed to the crowd: "If you must surrender, kill me first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongfu proclaimed to the crowd: "If you mean to surrender, kill me first.

sentences.zh: ”中設伏紿約議事，斬忠輔首擲陴外以示金人。
