translations.literal: " Zhong set an ambush and deceived him under pretense of discussing affairs; he beheaded Zhongfu and threw the head outside the walls to show the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhong set an ambush and lured him under pretense of discussing affairs, then beheaded Zhongfu and threw his head outside the walls to show the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 既開城門，可與不屈見殺。

translations.literal: After the gates were opened, Keyu refused to submit and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: After the gates were opened, Keyu refused to submit and was killed.

sentences.zh: 可與兄可求建炎中言於朝，官可與之子五人，而忠輔不與，士論惜之。

translations.literal: Keyu's elder brother Keqiu spoke to the court during Jianyan, and five of Keyu's sons were given office, but Zhongfu received nothing—scholars lamented this.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyan, Keyu's elder brother Keqiu spoke to the court, and five of Keyu's sons were given office, but Zhongfu received nothing. Scholars lamented the omission.

sentences.zh: 李彥仙，字少嚴，初名孝忠，寧州彭原人，徙鞏州。

translations.literal: Li Yansian, styled Shaoyan, originally named Xiaozhong, was from Pengyuan in Ningzhou and later moved to Gongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yansian, styled Shaoyan, originally named Xiaozhong, was from Pengyuan in Ningzhou and later moved to Gongzhou.

sentences.zh: 有大誌，所交皆豪俠士。

translations.literal: He had great ambition and associated only with bold and chivalrous men.
translations.idiomatic: He had great ambition and kept company only with bold and chivalrous men.

sentences.zh: 閑騎射。

translations.literal: In leisure he practiced mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In his leisure he practiced mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 家極邊，每出必陰察山川形勢，或間敵人縱牧，取其善馬以歸。

translations.literal: His home was on the far frontier. Whenever he went out he secretly surveyed the terrain of mountains and rivers, and occasionally when enemies pastured their herds he would take their best horses and return home.
translations.idiomatic: His home lay on the far frontier. Whenever he went abroad he secretly surveyed the lay of mountains and rivers, and now and then, when enemy herds were grazing, he would seize their best horses and ride home.

sentences.zh: 嚐為種師中部曲，入雲中，獲首級，補校尉。

translations.literal: He once served as a soldier under Zhong Shizhong, entered Yunzhong, took enemy heads, and was appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He once served under Zhong Shizhong, entered Yunzhong, took enemy heads, and was appointed company commander.

sentences.zh: 靖康元年，金人犯境，郡縣募兵勤王，遂率士應募，補承節郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingkang, when the Jurchens invaded the borders, the prefectures and counties raised troops to aid the throne; he then led men to enlist and was appointed Gentleman for Cherishing Integrity.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingkang, when the Jurchens invaded the borders, the prefectures and counties raised troops to aid the throne. He led men to enlist and was appointed Gentleman for Cherishing Integrity.

sentences.zh: 李綱宣撫兩河，上書言綱不知兵，恐誤國。

translations.literal: When Li Gang was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Two He, he submitted a memorial saying Gang did not understand warfare and would likely harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gang was appointed Pacification Commissioner for the Two He, he submitted a memorial saying that Gang did not understand warfare and would likely harm the state.

sentences.zh: 書聞，下有司追捕，乃亡去，易名彥仙。

translations.literal: When the memorial was received, orders went down to the relevant offices to pursue and arrest him, so he fled and changed his name to Yansian.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the court, orders went down to the relevant offices to pursue and arrest him. He fled and changed his name to Yansian.

sentences.zh: 以效用從河東軍，諜金人還，復補校尉。

translations.literal: For meritorious service he followed the Hedong army, returned after reconnoitering the Jurchens, and was again appointed company commander.
translations.idiomatic: For meritorious service he followed the Hedong army, returned after scouting the Jurchens, and was again appointed company commander.

sentences.zh: 河東陷，彥仙拔歸，道出陝，以兵事見守臣李彌大，彌大與語，壯之，留為裨將，戍淆、澠間。

translations.literal: When Hedong fell, Yansian fought his way back. Passing through Shaanxi he presented himself on military affairs to the defending official Li Mida; Mida spoke with him, was impressed, kept him as a deputy general, and garrisoned him between Xiao and Mian.
translations.idiomatic: When Hedong fell, Yansian fought his way back. Passing through Shaanxi he presented himself on military affairs to the defending official Li Mida. Mida spoke with him, was impressed, kept him as a deputy general, and garrisoned him between Xiao and Mian.

sentences.zh: 金人再犯汴，永興帥範致虛合西兵入援，彥仙遮說曰：“淆、澠道隘難以眾進，不若分兵而前，留其半於陝，可為後圖。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens again invaded Bian, Fan Zhixu, military commissioner of Yongxing, united the western troops to enter as relief. Yansian intercepted and advised: "The route through Xiao and Mian is narrow and difficult for a large force. Better to divide the army and advance, leaving half in Shaan—this would preserve options for the future.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens again invaded Bian, Fan Zhixu, military commissioner of Yongxing, united the western troops to march in relief. Yansian intercepted him and advised: "The route through Xiao and Mian is narrow and hard for a large force to pass. Better to divide the army and advance, leaving half in Shaan—this would preserve options for the future.

sentences.zh: ”致虛怒其沮眾，罷遣之。

translations.literal: " Zhixu was angered that he was dampening morale and dismissed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhixu was angered that he was dampening morale and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 師至千秋鎮，果敗，官吏皆遁。

translations.literal: The army reached Qianqiu garrison and was indeed defeated; the officials all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Qianqiu garrison and was indeed defeated. The officials all fled.

sentences.zh: 時彥仙為石壕尉，堅守三觜，民爭依之。

translations.literal: At that time Yansian was magistrate of Shihao and held firm at Sanzui; the people vied to take shelter with him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yansian was magistrate of Shihao and held firm at Sanzui. The people vied to take shelter with him.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：“尉異縣人，非如汝室墓於是。

translations.literal: He issued an order: "Your magistrate is from another county—I do not have family tombs here as you do.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "Your magistrate is from another county. I do not have family tombs here as you do.

sentences.zh: 今尉為汝守，若不悉力，金人將屍汝於市。

translations.literal: Now I am defending this place for you. If you do not exert yourselves fully, the Jurchens will pile your corpses in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am defending this place for you. If you do not exert yourselves fully, the Jurchens will pile your corpses in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: ”眾皆奮。

translations.literal: " The crowd all stirred with resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd all stirred with resolve.

sentences.zh: 金人攻三觜，彥仙戰佯北，金人追之，伏發，掩殺千計，分兵四出，下五十餘壁。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens attacked Sanzui, Yansian feigned defeat in battle; the Jurchens pursued, ambushers sprang up, and they slaughtered them by the thousand. He sent troops out in four directions and captured more than fifty fortified positions.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens attacked Sanzui, Yansian feigned defeat in battle. The Jurchens pursued, ambushers sprang up, and they slaughtered them by the thousand. He sent troops out in four directions and captured more than fifty fortified positions.

sentences.zh: 初，金人得陝，用降者守之，使招集散亡，彥仙陰遣士廁其間，金人不覺。

translations.literal: Initially when the Jurchens took Shaanzhou they used defectors to garrison it and had them gather scattered refugees. Yansian secretly sent men to mingle among them, and the Jurchens did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when the Jurchens took Shaanzhou they used defectors to garrison it and had them gather scattered refugees. Yansian secretly sent men to mingle among them, and the Jurchens did not notice.

sentences.zh: 乃引兵攻其南郭，夜潛師薄東北隅，所納士內應，噪而入，復陝州。

translations.literal: He then led troops to attack the southern suburb; by night he secretly moved his force close to the northeast corner, the men he had planted inside responded, and with a clamor they entered and recovered Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then led troops to attack the southern suburb. By night he secretly moved his force close to the northeast corner; the men he had planted inside responded, and with a clamor they entered and recovered Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 乘勝渡河，列柵中條諸山，旁郡邑皆響附，分遣邵雲等下絳、解諸邑。

translations.literal: Riding the victory he crossed the river, set palisades on the mountains of the Zhongtiao range, and neighboring prefectures and counties all rallied to him; he dispatched Shao Yun and others to take Jiang and Jie and various counties.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the victory he crossed the river and set palisades on the mountains of the Zhongtiao range. Neighboring prefectures and counties all rallied to him, and he dispatched Shao Yun and others to take Jiang, Jie, and various counties.

sentences.zh: 吏行文書，請州印章，彥仙曰：“吾以尉守此，第用吾印。

translations.literal: Officials sent documents requesting the prefecture seal. Yansian said: "I hold this place as a county magistrate—my own seal will suffice.
translations.idiomatic: Officials sent documents requesting the prefecture seal. Yansian said: "I hold this place as a county magistrate. My own seal will suffice.

sentences.zh: ”事聞，上謂輔臣曰：“近知彥仙與金人戰，再三獲捷，朕喜而不寐。

translations.literal: " When word reached the court, the emperor said to his chief ministers: "I have lately learned that Yansian has fought the Jurchens and won victories again and again—I am so pleased I cannot sleep.
translations.idiomatic: " When word reached the court, the emperor said to his chief ministers: "I have lately learned that Yansian has fought the Jurchens and won victories again and again. I am so pleased I cannot sleep.

sentences.zh: ”即命知陝州兼安撫使，遷武節郎、閣門宣讚舍人。

translations.literal: " He was immediately appointed prefect of Shaanzhou and concurrently Pacification Commissioner, and promoted to Gentleman of Martial Integrity and Gatehouse Attendant for Proclaiming Commendations.
translations.idiomatic: " He was immediately appointed prefect of Shaanzhou and concurrently Pacification Commissioner, and promoted to Gentleman of Martial Integrity and Gatehouse Attendant for Proclaiming Commendations.

sentences.zh: 彥仙搜軍實，增陴浚湟，益為戰守備，盡取家屬以來，曰：“吾以家徇國，與城俱存亡。

translations.literal: Yansian examined military resources, raised walls and dredged moats, and further strengthened preparations for battle and defense. He brought all his family members there and said: "I offer my family to the state—I rise and fall with the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian examined military resources, raised walls and dredged moats, and further strengthened preparations for battle and defense. He brought all his family members to the city and said: "I offer my family to the state. I rise and fall with the city.

sentences.zh: ”聞者感服。

translations.literal: " Those who heard were moved and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Those who heard were moved and submitted.

sentences.zh: 邵興在神稷山，以其眾來，願受節製。

translations.literal: Shao Xing was at Mount Shenji; he came with his troops and wished to accept Yansian's command.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xing was at Mount Shenji. He came with his troops and wished to accept Yansian's command.

sentences.zh: 彥仙辟興統領河北忠義軍馬，屯三門，後賴其力復虢州。

translations.literal: Yansian appointed Xing to command the loyalist army and cavalry of Hebei, garrisoned at Sanmen, and later relied on his strength to recover Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian appointed Xing to command the loyalist army and cavalry of Hebei and garrisoned him at Sanmen. Later he relied on Xing's strength to recover Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 金將烏魯撒拔再攻陝，彥仙極力禦之，金人技窮而去。

translations.literal: The Jurchen general Wulusaba again attacked Shaan, and Yansian resisted with all his might; when the Jurchens exhausted their tactics they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchen general Wulusaba again attacked Shaan, and Yansian resisted with all his might. When the Jurchens exhausted their tactics they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 三年，婁宿悉兵自蒲、解大入，彥仙伏兵中條山擊之，金兵大潰，婁宿僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the third year, Lousu led all his troops in a major invasion from Pu and Jie; Yansian ambushed them on Zhongtiao Mountain, the Jurchen army routed in great disorder, and Lousu barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, Lousu led all his troops in a major invasion from Pu and Jie. Yansian ambushed them on Zhongtiao Mountain, the Jurchen army routed in great disorder, and Lousu barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 授右武大夫、寧州觀察使兼同、虢州製置。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Militia Grand Master, Observation Commissioner of Ningzhou, and concurrently Commissioner for Tong and Guo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Militia Grand Master, Observation Commissioner of Ningzhou, and concurrently Commissioner for Tong and Guo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 彥仙度金人必並力來攻，即遣人詣宣撫使張浚求三千騎，俟金人攻陝，即空城度河北趨晉、絳、並、汾，搗其心腹，金人必自救，乃繇嵐、石西渡河，道鄜、延以歸。

translations.literal: Yansian judged the Jurchens would certainly concentrate their forces to attack. He immediately sent envoys to Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun requesting three thousand cavalry; when the Jurchens attacked Shaan, they would empty the city, cross north of the Yellow River toward Jin, Jiang, Bing, and Fen, strike at the enemy heartland—the Jurchens would surely rescue themselves—then return via Lan and Shi, cross west of the river, pass through Fuzhou and Yanzhou, and come back.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian judged that the Jurchens would certainly concentrate their forces to attack. He immediately sent envoys to Pacification Commissioner Zhang Jun requesting three thousand cavalry so that, when the Jurchens attacked Shaan, they could empty the city, cross north of the Yellow River toward Jin, Jiang, Bing, and Fen, and strike at the enemy heartland. The Jurchens would surely turn to save themselves, and his force could then return via Lan and Shi, cross west of the river, pass through Fuzhou and Yanzhou, and come back.

sentences.zh: 浚貽書勸彥仙空城清野，據險保聚，俟隙而動。

translations.literal: Jun sent a letter advising Yansian to empty the city and clear the countryside, hold fast in fortified places, and wait for an opening to act.
translations.idiomatic: Jun sent a letter advising Yansian to empty the city and clear the countryside, hold fast in fortified places, and wait for an opening to act.

sentences.zh: 彥仙不從。

translations.literal: Yansian did not comply.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian did not comply.

sentences.zh: 婁宿率叛將折可求眾號十萬來攻，分其軍為十，以正月旦為始，日輪一軍攻城，聚十軍並攻，期以三旬必拔。

translations.literal: Lousu led the defector general Zhe Keqiu and a force claiming one hundred thousand to attack. He divided his army into ten; starting from New Year's Day one army would attack the city each day in rotation, then gather all ten armies for a combined assault, setting a deadline of thirty days to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Lousu led the defector general Zhe Keqiu and a force claiming one hundred thousand to attack. He divided his army into ten. Starting from New Year's Day one army would attack the city each day in rotation, then all ten armies would attack together, with a deadline of thirty days to take it.

sentences.zh: 彥仙意氣如平常，登譙門，大作技樂，潛使人縋而出，焚其攻具，金人愕而卻。

translations.literal: Yansian's spirit was as usual. He ascended the watchtower gate and staged great performances of music and acrobatics; secretly he had men lowered over the walls to burn their siege equipment, and the Jurchens stood astonished and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian's spirit was as usual. He ascended the watchtower gate and staged great performances of music and acrobatics, while secretly having men lowered over the walls to burn the Jurchens' siege equipment. The Jurchens stood astonished and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 食盡，煮豆以啖其下，而取汁自飲。

translations.literal: When food ran out, he boiled beans to feed his subordinates while drinking the broth himself.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out, he boiled beans to feed his subordinates while drinking the broth himself.

sentences.zh: 至是亦盡，告急於浚，浚間道以金幣使犒其軍，檄都統製曲端涇原兵來援。

translations.literal: By then that too was exhausted. He sent urgent word to Jun; Jun sent an envoy by a secret route with gold and silks to reward the army, and issued orders for Commander-in-Chief Qu Duan's Jingyuan troops to come to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: By then that too was exhausted. He sent urgent word to Jun. Jun sent an envoy by a secret route with gold and silks to reward the army, and issued orders for Commander-in-Chief Qu Duan's Jingyuan troops to come to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 端素疾彥仙出己上，無出兵意。

translations.literal: Duan had long resented that Yansian outranked him and had no intention of sending troops.
translations.idiomatic: Duan had long resented that Yansian outranked him and had no intention of sending troops.

sentences.zh: 浚幕官謝升言於浚曰：“金旦暮下陝，則全據大河，且窺蜀矣。

translations.literal: Jun's staff officer Xie Sheng said to Jun: "If the Jurchens take Shaan any day now, they will control the entire Great River and moreover turn their gaze toward Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's staff officer Xie Sheng said to Jun: "If the Jurchens take Shaan any day now, they will control the entire Great River and moreover turn their gaze toward Shu.

sentences.zh: ”浚乃出師至長安。

translations.literal: " Jun thereupon marched out to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun thereupon marched out to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 道阻不得進，裨將邵隆、呂圓登、楊伯孫自外來援，間關傷仆，僅有至者。

translations.literal: The road was blocked and he could not advance. Deputy generals Shao Long, Lü Yuandeng, and Yang Bosun came from outside to reinforce; battered and wounded along the perilous route, only a few arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The road was blocked and he could not advance. Deputy generals Shao Long, Lü Yuandeng, and Yang Bosun came from outside to reinforce, but battered and wounded along the perilous route, only a few arrived.

sentences.zh: 彥仙日與金人戰，將士未嚐解甲。

translations.literal: Yansian fought the Jurchens day after day; the officers and soldiers never once removed their armor.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian fought the Jurchens day after day. The officers and soldiers never once removed their armor.

sentences.zh: 婁宿雅奇彥仙才，嚐啖以河南兵馬元帥，彥仙斬其使。

translations.literal: Lousu had long admired Yansian's talent and once tempted him with the post of Marshal of Henan troops and horses; Yansian beheaded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Lousu had long admired Yansian's talent and once tempted him with the post of Marshal of Henan troops and horses. Yansian beheaded the envoy.

sentences.zh: 至是使人呼曰：“即降，畀前秩。

translations.literal: At this time he sent a man to call out: "Surrender now and I will restore your former rank.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he sent a man to call out: "Surrender now and I will restore your former rank.

sentences.zh: ”彥仙曰：“吾寧為宋鬼，安用汝富貴為！

translations.literal: " Yansian said: "I would rather be a ghost of Song—what use have I for your wealth and rank!
translations.idiomatic: " Yansian said: "I would rather be a ghost of Song. What use have I for your wealth and rank!

sentences.zh: ”命強弩一發斃之。

translations.literal: " He ordered a powerful crossbow; one shot killed the messenger.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered a powerful crossbow fired. One shot killed the messenger.

sentences.zh: 設鉤索，日鉤取金人，舂斮城上。

translations.literal: They set grappling hooks and lines, each day hauling up Jurchens and pounding them to pieces atop the walls.
translations.idiomatic: They set grappling hooks and lines, each day hauling up Jurchens and pounding them to pieces atop the walls.

sentences.zh: 殺傷相當，守陴者傷夷日盡，金益兵急攻，城陷，彥仙率眾巷戰，矢集身如蝟，左臂中刃不斷，戰愈力。

translations.literal: Casualties were about equal; the defenders on the walls dwindled daily from wounds. The Jurchens reinforced and pressed the attack fiercely. The city fell. Yansian led the crowd in street fighting; arrows clustered on his body like a hedgehog. His left arm was struck by a blade but not severed, and he fought all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Casualties were about equal, and the defenders on the walls dwindled daily from wounds. The Jurchens reinforced and pressed the attack fiercely. The city fell. Yansian led the crowd in street fighting; arrows clustered on his body like a hedgehog. His left arm was struck by a blade but not severed, and he fought all the harder.

sentences.zh: 金人惜其才，以重賞募人生致之，彥仙易敝衣走渡河，曰：“吾不甘以身受敵人之刃。

translations.literal: The Jurchens prized his talent and offered rich rewards to anyone who could capture him alive. Yansian changed into worn clothes and fled to cross the river, saying: "I will not willingly let the enemy's blade take my body.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens prized his talent and offered rich rewards to anyone who could capture him alive. Yansian changed into worn clothes and fled to cross the river, saying: "I will not willingly let the enemy's blade take my body.

sentences.zh: ”既而聞金人縱兵屠掠，曰：“金人所以甘心此城，以我堅守不下故也，我何面目復生乎？

translations.literal: " Then he heard the Jurchens had let their troops slaughter and plunder, and said: "The Jurchens are so set on this city precisely because I held it and would not fall—what face have I to live on?
translations.idiomatic: " Then he heard the Jurchens had let their troops slaughter and plunder, and said: "The Jurchens are so set on this city precisely because I held it and would not fall. What face have I to live on?

sentences.zh: ”遂投河死，年三十六。

translations.literal: " He then threw himself into the river and died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: " He then threw himself into the river and died, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 金人害其家，惟弟夔、子毅得免。

translations.literal: The Jurchens destroyed his family; only his younger brother Kui and his son Yi escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens destroyed his family. Only his younger brother Kui and his son Yi escaped.

sentences.zh: 浚承製贈彥仙彰武軍節度使，建廟商州，號忠烈。

translations.literal: Jun, acting under imperial decree, posthumously granted Yansian Military Commissioner of Zhangwu Army, built a temple in Shangzhou, and gave him the title Loyal and Valiant.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, acting under imperial decree, posthumously granted Yansian the title of Military Commissioner of Zhangwu Army, built a temple in Shangzhou, and gave him the honorific Loyal and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 官其子，給宅一區，田五頃。

translations.literal: His son was given office, a residence, and five qing of farmland.
translations.idiomatic: His son was given office, a residence, and five qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，宣撫使周聿請即陝州立廟，名義烈。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, Pacification Commissioner Zhou Yu requested that a temple be established at Shaanzhou, named Righteous and Valiant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, Pacification Commissioner Zhou Yu requested that a temple be established at Shaanzhou, named Righteous and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 後以商、陝與金人，徙其廟閬州。

translations.literal: Later when Shang and Shaan were ceded to the Jurchens, the temple was moved to Langzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shang and Shaan were ceded to the Jurchens, the temple was moved to Langzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道八年，易諡忠威。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Qiandao, his posthumous title was changed to Loyal and Martial.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Qiandao, his posthumous title was changed to Loyal and Martial.

sentences.zh: 彥仙頎而長麵，嚴厲不可犯，以信義治陝，犯令者雖貴不貸。

translations.literal: Yansian was tall with a long face, stern and not to be transgressed. He governed Shaan by faith and righteousness; whoever violated orders, however high their rank, was not spared.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian was tall with a long face, stern and not to be transgressed. He governed Shaan by faith and righteousness, and whoever violated orders, however high their rank, was not spared.

sentences.zh: 與其下同甘苦，故士樂為用。

translations.literal: He shared hardship and comfort with his subordinates, so the soldiers gladly served him.
translations.idiomatic: He shared hardship and comfort with his subordinates, so the soldiers gladly served him.

sentences.zh: 有籌略，善應變。

translations.literal: He had stratagems and was skilled at adapting to circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: He had stratagems and was skilled at adapting to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 嚐略地至青澗，猝遇金人，眾愕眙，彥仙依山植疑幟，徐據柳林，解甲自如。

translations.literal: Once while reconnoitering he reached Qingjian and suddenly encountered Jurchens. The men stared in shock. Yansian planted deceptive banners on the hillside, slowly took position in a willow grove, and removed his armor as if at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once while reconnoitering he reached Qingjian and suddenly encountered Jurchens. The men stared in shock. Yansian planted deceptive banners on the hillside, slowly took position in a willow grove, and removed his armor as if at ease.

sentences.zh: 金人疑有伏，引去，彥仙追襲於隘，躪死相枕。

translations.literal: The Jurchens suspected an ambush and withdrew; Yansian pursued and struck them at a narrow pass, where the dead piled atop one another from trampling.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens suspected an ambush and withdrew. Yansian pursued and struck them at a narrow pass, where the dead piled atop one another from trampling.

sentences.zh: 關以東皆下，陝獨存，金人必欲下陝，然後並力西向。

translations.literal: All east of the passes had fallen; only Shaan still held. The Jurchens had to take Shaan before they could concentrate their strength westward.
translations.idiomatic: All east of the passes had fallen; only Shaan still held. The Jurchens had to take Shaan before they could concentrate their strength westward.

sentences.zh: 彥仙以孤城扼其衝再逾年，大小二百戰，金人不得西。

translations.literal: Yansian with a lone city blocked their thrust for more than another year, fighting two hundred engagements large and small, and the Jurchens could not advance west.
translations.idiomatic: With a lone city Yansian blocked their thrust for more than another year, fighting two hundred engagements large and small, and the Jurchens could not advance west.

sentences.zh: 至城陷，民無貳心，雖婦女亦升屋以瓦擲金人，哭李觀察不絕。

translations.literal: When the city finally fell the people harbored no divided loyalty; even women climbed onto rooftops to hurl tiles at the Jurchens, wailing without cease for Inspector Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the city finally fell the people harbored no divided loyalty. Even women climbed onto rooftops to hurl tiles at the Jurchens, wailing without cease for Inspector Li.

sentences.zh: 金人怒，屠其城，全陝遂沒。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were enraged and slaughtered the city; all of Shaan was lost.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were enraged and slaughtered the city. All of Shaan was lost.

sentences.zh: 裨將邵雲、呂圓登、宋炎、賈何、閻平、趙成皆死，並贈官錄其家。

translations.literal: Deputy generals Shao Yun, Lü Yuandeng, Song Yan, Jia He, Yan Ping, and Zhao Cheng all died and were posthumously given office; their families were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy generals Shao Yun, Lü Yuandeng, Song Yan, Jia He, Yan Ping, and Zhao Cheng all died and were posthumously given office. Their families were enrolled.

sentences.zh: 邵雲，龍門人。

translations.literal: Shao Yun was a native of Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Yun was a native of Longmen.

sentences.zh: 金人陷蒲城，雲聚少年數百，壁山谷，時出撓之。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens took Pucheng, Yun gathered several hundred young men, fortified themselves in a mountain valley, and sallied out from time to time to harass them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens took Pucheng, Yun gathered several hundred young men, fortified themselves in a mountain valley, and sallied out from time to time to harass them.

sentences.zh: 會邵隆起兵，雲往從之，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: When Shao Long raised troops, Yun went to join him and they pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: When Shao Long raised troops, Yun went to join him and they pledged brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 聞胡夜義者眾強，乃舉所部聽命。

translations.literal: Hearing that Hu Yeyi had a large and powerful force, he brought his entire command to accept Yeyi's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Hu Yeyi had a large and powerful force, he brought his entire command to accept Yeyi's orders.

sentences.zh: 李彥仙嚐假夜義官，夜義意不滿，掠南原而去，彥仙誘殺之。

translations.literal: Li Yansian had once lent Yeyi an office title; Yeyi was displeased, plundered the southern plain and departed, and Yansian lured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yansian had once lent Yeyi an office title. Yeyi was displeased, plundered the southern plain and departed, and Yansian lured and killed him.

sentences.zh: 雲欲攻陝，彥仙遣客說以義，遂來歸。

translations.literal: Yun intended to attack Shaan; Yansian sent an envoy to persuade him with righteousness, and he came over to Yansian's side.
translations.idiomatic: Yun intended to attack Shaan. Yansian sent an envoy to persuade him with righteousness, and he came over to Yansian's side.

sentences.zh: 累有功，官至武翼郎、閣門宣讚舍人。

translations.literal: He accumulated merit repeatedly and rose to Gentleman of Martial Feathers and Gatehouse Attendant for Proclaiming Commendations.
translations.idiomatic: He accumulated merit repeatedly and rose to Gentleman of Martial Feathers and Gatehouse Attendant for Proclaiming Commendations.

sentences.zh: 城破被執，婁宿欲命以千戶長，雲大罵不屈，婁宿怒，釘雲五日而磔之。

translations.literal: When the city fell he was captured. Lousu wished to appoint him leader of a thousand households; Yun cursed him loudly and refused to submit. Lousu was enraged, nailed Yun up for five days, and then dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he was captured. Lousu wished to appoint him leader of a thousand households, but Yun cursed him loudly and refused to submit. Lousu was enraged, nailed Yun up for five days, and then dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 金人有就視者，猶咀血噴其面，至抉眼摘肝，罵不絕。

translations.literal: When Jurchens came to look at him, he still chewed blood and spat it in their faces, even gouging out eyes and tearing out livers, cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchens came to look in on him, he still chewed blood and spat it in their faces, even gouging out eyes and tearing out livers, and cursed without cease.

sentences.zh: 呂圓登，夏縣人。

translations.literal: Lü Yuandeng was a native of Xia County.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yuandeng was a native of Xia County.

sentences.zh: 嚐為僧，後以良家子應募，捍金人淆、澠間。

translations.literal: He had once been a monk; later he enlisted as a commoner and defended the region between the Xiao and Mian Rivers against the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: He had once been a monk. Later he enlisted as a commoner and defended the region between the Xiao and Mian Rivers against the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 彥仙保三觜，圓登歸之，功最多，為愛將。

translations.literal: Yansian held Sanzui; Yuandeng joined him, achieved the most merit, and became a favored general.
translations.idiomatic: Yansian held Sanzui. Yuandeng joined him, achieved the most merit, and became a favored general.

sentences.zh: 城垂破，以兵來援，身重創，持彥仙泣曰：“圍久，不知公安否，今得見公，且死無恨。

translations.literal: When the city was on the verge of falling, he came with troops to reinforce it. Badly wounded, he grasped Yansian and wept, saying, "The siege has lasted so long that I did not know whether you were safe. Now that I have seen you, I can die without regret.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was on the verge of falling, he came with troops to reinforce it. Badly wounded, he grasped Yansian and wept, saying, "The siege has lasted so long that I did not know whether you were safe. Now that I have seen you, I can die without regret.

sentences.zh: ”創身方臥，聞城陷，遽起戰死。

translations.literal: " His wounded body had just lain down when he heard that the city had fallen; he sprang up at once and died fighting.
translations.idiomatic: " His wounded body had just lain down when he heard that the city had fallen. He sprang up at once and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 宋炎，陝縣人。

translations.literal: Song Yan was a native of Shaan County.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yan was a native of Shaan County.

sentences.zh: 蹶張命中，補秉義郎。

translations.literal: Skilled at drawing the crossbow with the foot, he was appointed Gentleman Defender of Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at drawing the crossbow with the foot, he was appointed Gentleman Defender of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 先，金人圍城，炎射死數百人。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Jurchens besieged the city, Yan shot several hundred men dead.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Jurchens besieged the city, Yan shot several hundred men dead.

sentences.zh: 比再圍，炎以勁弩數百，發毒矢殺千餘人。

translations.literal: When they besieged it again, Yan with several hundred powerful crossbows loosed poisoned bolts and killed more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When they besieged it again, Yan used several hundred powerful crossbows to loose poisoned bolts and killed more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 城陷，金人聲言求善射者貴之，炎不應，力戰死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the Jurchens publicly announced that they sought skilled archers and would honor them richly; Yan did not respond and died fighting to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, the Jurchens publicly announced that they sought skilled archers and would honor them richly. Yan did not respond and died fighting to the end.

sentences.zh: 趙立，徐州張益村人。

translations.literal: Zhao Li was a native of Zhangyi Village in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Li was a native of Zhangyi Village in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 以敢勇隸兵籍。

translations.literal: Because of his bold courage he was enrolled in the military registers.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his bold courage he was enrolled in the military registers.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，金人大入，盜賊群起，立數有戰功，為武衛都虞候。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, when the Jurchens invaded on a great scale and bandits rose everywhere, Li repeatedly won battle merit and became chief adjutant of the Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, when the Jurchens invaded on a great scale and bandits rose everywhere, Li repeatedly won battle merit and became chief adjutant of the Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，金人攻徐，王復拒守，命立督戰，中六矢，戰益厲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, when the Jurchens attacked Xu, Wang Fu held the defense and ordered Li to direct the fighting. Li was struck by six arrows but fought all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, when the Jurchens attacked Xu, Wang Fu held the defense and ordered Li to direct the fighting. Li was struck by six arrows but fought all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 復壯其勇，酌卮酒揮涕勞之。

translations.literal: Fu admired his courage, poured a cup of wine, wiped away tears, and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu admired his courage, poured him a cup of wine, wiped away tears, and rewarded him.

sentences.zh: 城陷，復與其家皆死，獨子佾先去。

translations.literal: When the city fell, Fu and his whole household died; only his son Yi escaped beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, Fu and his whole household died. Only his son Yi escaped beforehand.

sentences.zh: 州教授鄭褒亦罵敵而死。

translations.literal: The prefectural instructor Zheng Bao also cursed the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural instructor Zheng Bao also cursed the enemy and died.

sentences.zh: 城始破，立巷戰，奪門以出，金人擊之死，夜半得微雨而蘇，乃殺守者，入城求復屍，慟哭手瘞之。

translations.literal: When the city was first breached, Li fought through the alleys, seized a gate, and got out; the Jurchens struck him down and he died. At midnight a light rain fell and he revived. He then killed the guards, entered the city to seek Fu's corpse, wept in grief, and buried it with his own hands.
translations.idiomatic: When the city was first breached, Li fought through the alleys, seized a gate, and got out. The Jurchens struck him down and he died. At midnight a light rain fell and he revived. He then killed the guards, entered the city to seek Fu's corpse, wept in grief, and buried it with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 陰結鄉民為收復計。

translations.literal: In secret he rallied the local people to plan recovery.
translations.idiomatic: In secret he rallied the local people to plan the city's recovery.

sentences.zh: 金人北還，立率殘兵邀擊，斷其歸路，奪舟船金帛以千計，軍聲復振。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens withdrew north, Li led remnant troops to intercept them, cut off their route of retreat, and seized boats, gold, and silk by the thousands; the army's reputation revived.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens withdrew north, Li led remnant troops to intercept them, cut off their route of retreat, and seized boats, gold, and silk by the thousands. The army's reputation revived.

sentences.zh: 乃盡結鄉民為兵，遂復徐州。

translations.literal: He then rallied all the local people as soldiers and recovered Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He then rallied all the local people as soldiers and recovered Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔授忠翊郎、權知州事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Loyal Assistant Gentleman and acting prefect.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Loyal Assistant Gentleman and acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 立奏為復立廟，每遇歲時及出師，必帥眾泣禱曰：“公為朝廷死，必能陰祐其遺民也。

translations.literal: Li memorialized the throne to establish a temple for Fu. Every year at the seasonal rites and whenever troops set out, he would lead the people in tearful prayer, saying, "You died for the court and will surely give hidden protection to the people you left behind.
translations.idiomatic: Li memorialized the throne to establish a temple for Fu. Every year at the seasonal rites and whenever troops set out, he would lead the people in tearful prayer, saying, "You died for the court and will surely give hidden protection to the people you left behind.

sentences.zh: ”齊人聞之歸心焉。

translations.literal: " When the people of Qi heard this, their hearts turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: " When the people of Qi heard this, their hearts turned to him.

sentences.zh: 時山東諸郡莽為盜區，立介居其間，威名流聞。

translations.literal: At that time the commanderies of Shandong had largely become bandit territory; Li stood among them, and his martial renown spread far.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the commanderies of Shandong had largely become bandit territory. Li stood among them, and his martial renown spread far.

sentences.zh: 累遷右武大夫、忠州刺史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Martial Righteousness and prefect of Zhongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of Martial Righteousness and prefect of Zhongzhou.

sentences.zh: 會金左將軍昌圍楚州急，通守賈敦詩欲以城降，宣撫使杜充命立將所部兵往赴之。

translations.literal: It happened that Chang, the Jin Left General, was pressing Chuzhou hard. The acting prefect Jia Dunshi wished to surrender the city. Pacification Commissioner Du Chong ordered Li to lead his troops there.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Chang, the Jin Left General, was pressing Chuzhou hard. The acting prefect Jia Dunshi wished to surrender the city, so Pacification Commissioner Du Chong ordered Li to lead his troops there.

sentences.zh: 且戰且行，連七戰勝而後能達楚。

translations.literal: Fighting as he marched, he won seven battles in succession before he could reach Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting as he marched, he won seven battles in succession before he could reach Chu.

sentences.zh: 兩頰中流矢，不能言，以手指麾，既入城休士，而後拔鏃。

translations.literal: Arrows struck both his cheeks and he could not speak; he directed with his fingers. Only after entering the city and resting the troops did he pull out the arrowheads.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows struck both his cheeks and he could not speak, so he directed with his fingers. Only after entering the city and resting the troops did he pull out the arrowheads.

sentences.zh: 詔以立守楚州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Li to defend Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Li to defend Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，金人攻城，立命撤廢屋，城下然火池，壯士持長矛以待。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, when the Jurchens attacked the city, he immediately ordered abandoned houses torn down, fires lit beneath the walls to form burning pools, and stalwart men to stand ready with long spears.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, when the Jurchens attacked the city, he immediately ordered abandoned houses torn down, fires lit beneath the walls to form burning pools, and stalwart men to stand ready with long spears.

sentences.zh: 金人登城，鉤取投火中。

translations.literal: When Jurchens climbed the wall, they were hooked and thrown into the fire.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurchens climbed the wall, they were hooked and thrown into the fire.

sentences.zh: 金人選死士突入，又搏殺之，乃稍引退。

translations.literal: The Jurchens selected death-defying warriors to break in, but they were beaten and killed as well, and the enemy then withdrew somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens selected death-defying warriors to break in, but they were beaten and killed as well, and the enemy then withdrew somewhat.

sentences.zh: 五月，兀術北歸，築高台六合，以輜重假道於楚，立斬其使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Wuzhu withdrew north, built a high platform at Liuhe, and sought to pass through Chu with his baggage train; Li executed his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Wuzhu withdrew north, built a high platform at Liuhe, and sought to pass through Chu with his baggage train. Li executed his envoy.

sentences.zh: 兀術怒，乃設南北兩屯，絕楚餉道，立引兵出戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Wuzhu was enraged and set up two camps north and south, cutting off Chu's supply route. Li led troops out to fight and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu was enraged and set up two camps north and south, cutting off Chu's supply route. Li led troops out to fight and routed them utterly.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷分鎮，以立為徐州觀察使、泗州漣水軍鎮撫使兼知楚州。

translations.literal: When the court divided the garrison commands, Li was made observation commissioner of Xuzhou, pacification commissioner of the Lianshui Army of Sizhou, and concurrently prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the court divided the garrison commands, Li was made observation commissioner of Xuzhou, pacification commissioner of the Lianshui Army of Sizhou, and concurrently prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 立一日擁六騎出城，呼曰：“我鎮撫也，可來接戰。

translations.literal: One day Li rode out of the city with six horsemen and shouted, "I am the pacification commissioner. Come and meet me in battle.
translations.idiomatic: One day Li rode out of the city with six horsemen and shouted, "I am the pacification commissioner. Come and meet me in battle.

sentences.zh: ”有兩騎將襲其背，立奮二矛刺之，俱墮地，奪兩馬而還。

translations.literal: " Two horsemen were about to strike from behind; Li brandished two spears and stabbed them. Both fell to the ground, and he seized their two horses and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Two horsemen were about to strike from behind. Li brandished two spears and stabbed them. Both fell to the ground, and he seized their two horses and returned.

sentences.zh: 眾數十追其後，立瞋目大呼，人馬皆辟易。

translations.literal: Several dozen men pursued behind him; Li glared and shouted loudly, and both men and horses shrank back.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen men pursued behind him. Li glared and shouted loudly, and both men and horses shrank back.

sentences.zh: 明日，金人列三隊邀戰，立為三陣應之，金人以鐵騎數百橫分其陣而圍之，立奮身突圍，持挺左右大呼，金人落馬者不知數。

translations.literal: The next day the Jurchens formed three ranks to offer battle; Li answered with three formations. The Jurchens sent several hundred armored horsemen to cut across his formation and surround it. Li threw himself forward to break out, wielding a club and shouting left and right; Jurchens knocked from their horses were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Jurchens formed three ranks to offer battle, and Li answered with three formations. The Jurchens sent several hundred armored horsemen to cut across his formation and surround it. Li threw himself forward to break out, wielding a club and shouting left and right. Jurchens knocked from their horses were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 承、楚間有樊梁、新開、白馬三湖，賊張敵萬窟穴其間，立絕不與通，故楚糧道愈梗。

translations.literal: Between Cheng and Chu lay the three lakes Fanliang, Xinkai, and Baima, where the bandit Zhang Diwan had his lairs. Li would have no dealings with him, so Chu's supply route grew ever more blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Between Cheng and Chu lay the three lakes Fanliang, Xinkai, and Baima, where the bandit Zhang Diwan had his lairs. Li would have no dealings with him, so Chu's supply route grew ever more blocked.

sentences.zh: 始受圍，菽麥野生，澤有鳧茨可采，後皆盡，至屑榆皮食之。

translations.literal: At first, when the siege began, beans and wheat grew wild and there were arrowhead plants in the marshes that could be gathered. Later all was exhausted, and they came even to eating shredded elm bark.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the siege began, beans and wheat grew wild and there were arrowhead plants in the marshes that could be gathered. Later all was exhausted, and they came even to eating shredded elm bark.

sentences.zh: 承州既陷，楚勢益孤，立遣人詣朝廷告急。

translations.literal: After Chengzhou had fallen, Chu's position grew ever more isolated, and Li sent men to the court to report the emergency.
translations.idiomatic: After Chengzhou had fallen, Chu's position grew ever more isolated, and Li sent men to the court to report the emergency.

sentences.zh: 簽書樞密院事趙鼎欲遣張俊救之，俊不肯行。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding, deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, wished to send Zhang Jun to rescue the city, but Jun refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding, deputy director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, wished to send Zhang Jun to rescue the city, but Jun refused to go.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：“江東新造，全藉兩淮，失楚則大事去矣。

translations.literal: Ding said, "The southeast has only just been established and depends entirely on the two Huai regions. If Chu is lost, the great enterprise is finished.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "The southeast has only just been established and depends entirely on the two Huai regions. If Chu is lost, the great enterprise is finished.

sentences.zh: 若俊憚行，臣願與之偕往。

translations.literal: If Jun fears to go, I am willing to go with him.
translations.idiomatic: If Jun fears to go, I am willing to go with him.

sentences.zh: ”俊復力辭，乃命劉光世督淮南諸鎮救楚。

translations.literal: " Jun again declined with all his strength, so Liu Guangshi was ordered to supervise the garrisons of Huainan in rescuing Chu.
translations.idiomatic: " Jun again declined with all his strength, so Liu Guangshi was ordered to supervise the garrisons of Huainan in rescuing Chu.

sentences.zh: 東海李彥先首以兵至淮河，扼不得進；

translations.literal: Li Yanxian of Donghai was the first to reach the Huai River with troops, but was blocked and could not advance;
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanxian of Donghai was the first to reach the Huai River with troops, but was blocked and could not advance;

sentences.zh: 高郵薛慶至揚州，轉戰被執死；

translations.literal: Xue Qing of Gaoyou reached Yangzhou, fought on in many battles, was captured, and died;
translations.idiomatic: Xue Qing of Gaoyou reached Yangzhou, fought on in many battles, was captured, and died;

sentences.zh: 光世將王德至承州，下不用命；

translations.literal: Wang De, a general under Guangshi, reached Chengzhou, but his subordinates would not obey orders;
translations.idiomatic: Wang De, a general under Guangshi, reached Chengzhou, but his subordinates would not obey orders;

sentences.zh: 揚州郭仲威按兵天長，陰懷顧望；

translations.literal: Guo Zhongwei of Yangzhou held his troops at Tianchang, secretly wavering and looking back;
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zhongwei of Yangzhou held his troops at Tianchang, secretly wavering and looking back;

sentences.zh: 獨海陵岳飛僅能為援，而眾寡不敵。

translations.literal: only Yue Fei of Hailing was able to offer aid, but his numbers were too few to match the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yue Fei of Hailing was able to offer aid, but his numbers were too few to match the enemy.

sentences.zh: 高宗覽立奏，歎曰：“立堅守孤城，雖古名將無以逾之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong read Li's memorial and sighed, saying, "Li has held a lone city to the end; even the great generals of old could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong read Li's memorial and sighed, saying, "Li has held a lone city to the end. Even the great generals of old could not surpass him.

sentences.zh: ”以書趣光世會兵者五，光世訖不行。

translations.literal: " He sent five letters urging Guangshi to assemble troops, but Guangshi never went.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent five letters urging Guangshi to assemble troops, but Guangshi never went.

sentences.zh: 金知外救絕，圍益急。

translations.literal: The Jurchens knew that outside relief was cut off and pressed the siege all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens knew that outside relief was cut off and pressed the siege all the more fiercely.

sentences.zh: 九月，攻東城，立募壯士焚其梯，火輒反向，立歎曰：“豈天未助順乎。

translations.literal: In the ninth month they attacked the eastern wall. Li recruited stalwart men to burn their scaling ladders, but the fire kept turning back on them. Li sighed and said, "Has Heaven not yet favored the righteous cause?
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they attacked the eastern wall. Li recruited stalwart men to burn their scaling ladders, but the fire kept turning back on them. Li sighed and said, "Has Heaven not yet favored the righteous cause?

sentences.zh: ”一旦風轉，焚一梯，立喜，登磴道以觀，飛炮中其首，左右馳救之，立曰：“我終不能為國殄賊矣。

translations.literal: " In a moment the wind shifted and one ladder was burned. Li rejoiced, climbed the ramp to watch, and a flying projectile struck his head. Those at his side rushed to save him. Li said, "I can never destroy the enemy for the state after all.
translations.idiomatic: " In a moment the wind shifted and one ladder was burned. Li rejoiced, climbed the ramp to watch, and a flying projectile struck his head. Those at his side rushed to save him. Li said, "I can never destroy the enemy for the state after all.

sentences.zh: ”言訖而絕，年三十有七。

translations.literal: " When he had finished speaking he died. He was thirty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: " When he had finished speaking he died. He was thirty-seven.

sentences.zh: 眾巷哭。

translations.literal: The people wept in the alleys.
translations.idiomatic: The people wept in the alleys.

sentences.zh: 以參謀官程括攝鎮撫使以守。

translations.literal: Staff officer Cheng Kuo was appointed acting pacification commissioner to hold the defense.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Cheng Kuo was appointed acting pacification commissioner to hold the defense.

sentences.zh: 金人疑立詐死，不敢動。

translations.literal: The Jurchens suspected that Li had feigned death and did not dare act.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens suspected that Li had feigned death and did not dare act.

sentences.zh: 越旬餘，城始陷。

translations.literal: More than ten days later the city finally fell.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days later the city finally fell.

sentences.zh: 初，朝廷聞楚乏食，與粟萬斛，命兩浙轉運李承造自海道先致三千斛，未發而楚失守矣。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the court heard that Chu lacked food, it granted ten thousand hu of grain and ordered Li Chenzao, transport commissioner of the Two Zhes, to send three thousand hu first by sea route, but before it was dispatched Chu had already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court heard that Chu lacked food, it granted ten thousand hu of grain and ordered Li Chenzao, transport commissioner of the Two Zhes, to send three thousand hu first by sea route, but before it was dispatched Chu had already fallen.

sentences.zh: 立家先殘於徐，以單騎入楚。

translations.literal: Li's family had already been destroyed at Xu; he entered Chu alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Li's family had already been destroyed at Xu. He entered Chu alone on a single horse.

sentences.zh: 為人木強，不知書，忠義出天性。

translations.literal: By nature he was stolid and unlearned, yet loyalty and righteousness came from within him.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was stolid and unlearned, yet loyalty and righteousness came from within him.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，不喜聲色財利，與士卒均廩給。

translations.literal: He was skilled at riding and archery, cared nothing for music, women, or profit, and shared rations equally with his soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at riding and archery, cared nothing for music, women, or profit, and shared rations equally with his soldiers.

sentences.zh: 每戰擐甲胄先登，有退卻者，大呼馳至，捽而斬之。

translations.literal: In every battle he donned armor and led the ascent first. If anyone fell back, he shouted and galloped up, seized him, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he donned armor and led the ascent first. If anyone fell back, he shouted and galloped up, seized him, and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 初入城，合徐、楚兵不滿萬，二州眾不相能，立善撫馭，無敢私隙。

translations.literal: When he first entered the city, the combined troops of Xu and Chu numbered fewer than ten thousand, and the men of the two prefectures did not get along. Li governed them well and allowed no private quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: When he first entered the city, the combined troops of Xu and Chu numbered fewer than ten thousand, and the men of the two prefectures did not get along. Li governed them well and allowed no private quarrels.

sentences.zh: 仇視金人，言之必嚼齒而怒，所俘獲磔以示眾，未嚐獻馘行在也。

translations.literal: He hated the Jurchens; whenever he spoke of them he ground his teeth in rage. Captives he dismembered to display before the troops, and he never once presented enemy heads to the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: He hated the Jurchens. Whenever he spoke of them he ground his teeth in rage. Captives he dismembered to display before the troops, and he never once presented enemy heads to the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 劉豫遣立故人齎書約降，立不發書，束以油布焚市中，且曰：“吾了此賊，必滅豫乃止。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent an old acquaintance of Li's bearing a letter inviting surrender. Li did not open the letter, bound it in oiled cloth, and burned it in the marketplace, saying, "When I have finished with these bandits, I will not stop until Yu is destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent an old acquaintance of Li's bearing a letter inviting surrender. Li did not open the letter, bound it in oiled cloth, and burned it in the marketplace, saying, "When I have finished with these bandits, I will not stop until Yu is destroyed.

sentences.zh: ”由是忠義之聲遠近皆傾下之，金人不敢斥其名。

translations.literal: " From this his reputation for loyalty and righteousness spread near and far, and all looked up to him. The Jurchens did not dare speak his name aloud.
translations.idiomatic: " From this his reputation for loyalty and righteousness spread near and far, and all looked up to him. The Jurchens did not dare speak his name aloud.

sentences.zh: 圍既久，眾益困，立夜焚香望東南拜，且泣曰：“誓死守，不敢負國家。

translations.literal: The siege had lasted long and the people grew ever more distressed. At night Li burned incense, bowed toward the southeast, and wept, saying, "I swear to hold to the death and dare not fail the state.
translations.idiomatic: The siege had lasted long and the people grew ever more distressed. At night Li burned incense, bowed toward the southeast, and wept, saying, "I swear to hold to the death and dare not fail the state.

sentences.zh: ”命其眾擊鼓，曰：“援兵至，聞吾鼓聲則應矣。

translations.literal: " He ordered his troops to beat drums and said, "When relief arrives, they will answer when they hear our drumbeats.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered his troops to beat drums and said, "When relief arrives, they will answer when they hear our drumbeats.

sentences.zh: ”如是累月，終無至者。

translations.literal: " This went on for months, but in the end none came.
translations.idiomatic: " This went on for months, but in the end none came.

sentences.zh: 立嚐戒士卒：不幸城破，必巷戰決死。

translations.literal: Li had once warned his soldiers: if the city should unhappily fall, they must fight to the death in the alleys.
translations.idiomatic: Li had once warned his soldiers that if the city should unhappily fall, they must fight to the death in the alleys.

sentences.zh: 及陷，眾如其言。

translations.literal: When it fell, the people did as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: When it fell, the people did as he had said.

sentences.zh: 自金人犯中國，所下城率以虛聲脅降，惟太原堅守逾二年，濮州城破，殺傷大相當，皆為金人所憚。

translations.literal: Since the Jurchens invaded China, the cities they took were generally coerced into surrender by empty threats. Only Taiyuan held firm for more than two years, and when Puzhou fell the casualties on both sides were nearly equal; both were feared by the Jurchens.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jurchens invaded China, the cities they took were generally coerced into surrender by empty threats. Only Taiyuan held firm for more than two years, and when Puzhou fell the casualties on both sides were nearly equal. Both were feared by the Jurchens.

sentences.zh: 而立威名戰多，鹹出其上。

translations.literal: As for Li, his martial renown and many battles exceeded them all.
translations.idiomatic: As for Li, his martial renown and many battles exceeded them all.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，輟朝，贈奉國節度使、開府儀同三司，官其子孫十人，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: When word of his death reached the court, audiences were suspended. He was posthumously given the title of military commissioner of Fengguo and Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies; ten of his descendants were given office, and he was given the posthumous name Loyal and Valiant.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached the court, audiences were suspended. He was posthumously given the title of military commissioner of Fengguo and Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies. Ten of his descendants were given office, and he was given the posthumous name Loyal and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 明年，金人退，得立屍譙樓下，頰骨箭穴存焉。

translations.literal: The next year, after the Jurchens withdrew, his corpse was found beneath the watchtower; the arrow wound in his cheekbone was still visible.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, after the Jurchens withdrew, his corpse was found beneath the watchtower. The arrow wound in his cheekbone was still visible.

sentences.zh: 命官給葬事，後為立祠，名曰顯忠。

translations.literal: Officials were ordered to provide the burial, and later a temple was established for Li, named Manifest Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to provide the burial, and later a temple was established for Li, named Manifest Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 王復，以龍圖閣待制知徐州。

translations.literal: Wang Fu served as prefect of Xuzhou with the title of Hanlin Academy attendant for the Hall of Dragon Designs.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fu served as prefect of Xuzhou with the title of Hanlin Academy attendant for the Hall of Dragon Designs.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年，金人自襲慶府引兵圍徐州，復與男倚同守城，率軍民力戰。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianyan, the Jurchens marched from Xiqing Prefecture to besiege Xuzhou. Fu and his son Yi defended the city together and led soldiers and civilians in fierce fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianyan, the Jurchens marched from Xiqing Prefecture to besiege Xuzhou. Fu and his son Yi defended the city together and led soldiers and civilians in fierce fighting.

sentences.zh: 外援不至，城陷，復堅坐聽事不去，謂粘罕曰：“死守者我也，監郡而次無預焉，願殺我而舍僚吏百姓。

translations.literal: Outside relief did not arrive and the city fell. Fu sat firmly in the audience hall and would not leave. He said to Nianhan, "It is I who held to the death. The supervising prefect and the rest had no part in it. I ask that you kill me and spare the officials and the people.
translations.idiomatic: Outside relief did not arrive and the city fell. Fu sat firmly in the audience hall and would not leave. He said to Nianhan, "It is I who held to the death. The supervising prefect and the rest had no part in it. I ask that you kill me and spare the officials and the people.

sentences.zh: ”粘罕欲降之，復慢罵求死，闔門百口皆被殺。

translations.literal: " Nianhan wished to make him submit, but Fu insulted him contemptuously and sought death. All one hundred members of his household were killed.
translations.idiomatic: " Nianhan wished to make him submit, but Fu insulted him contemptuously and sought death. All one hundred members of his household were killed.

sentences.zh: 巡檢楊彭年亦死焉。

translations.literal: The patrol officer Yang Pengnian also died there.
translations.idiomatic: The patrol officer Yang Pengnian also died there.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈復資政殿學士，諡壯節，立廟楚州，號忠烈，官其家五人。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Fu was posthumously made an academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and given the posthumous name Valiant Integrity. A temple was established for him at Chuzhou, titled Loyal and Valiant, and five members of his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, Fu was posthumously made an academician of the Hall for Assisting Governance and given the posthumous name Valiant Integrity. A temple was established for him at Chuzhou, titled Loyal and Valiant, and five members of his family were given office.

sentences.zh: 王忠植，太行義士也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongzhi was a loyalist hero of the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongzhi was a loyalist hero of the Taihang Mountains.

sentences.zh: 紹興九年，取石州等十一郡，授武功大夫、華州觀察、統製河東忠義軍馬，遂知代州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, he took eleven prefectures including Shizhou. He was appointed Grand Master of Martial Achievement, observation commissioner of Huazhou, and commander of the loyalist troops and horses of Hedong, and then became prefect of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Shaoxing, he took eleven prefectures including Shizhou. He was appointed Grand Master of Martial Achievement, observation commissioner of Huazhou, and commander of the loyalist troops and horses of Hedong, and then became prefect of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 尋落階官，為建寧軍承宣使、龍神衛四廂都指揮使、河東經略安撫使。

translations.literal: Soon he was stripped of his rank-holding office and made commissioner of the Jianning Army, commander-in-chief of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, and pacification commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was stripped of his rank-holding office and made commissioner of the Jianning Army, commander-in-chief of the four wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, and pacification commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 明年，金人圍慶陽急，帥臣宋萬年乘城拒守。

translations.literal: The next year the Jurchens pressed Qingyang hard, and the commander Song Wannian mounted the wall to hold the defense.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Jurchens pressed Qingyang hard, and the commander Song Wannian mounted the wall to hold the defense.

sentences.zh: 會川、陝宣撫副使胡世將檄忠植以所部赴陝西會合，行次延安，叛將趙惟清執忠植使拜詔，忠植曰：“本朝詔則拜，金國詔則不拜。

translations.literal: Hu Shijiang, deputy pacification commissioner of Chuan and Shaan, ordered Zhongzhi to bring his troops to join forces in Shaanxi. On the march at Yan'an, the rebel general Zhao Weiqing seized Zhongzhi and forced him to bow to an edict. Zhongzhi said, "If it is an edict of our dynasty, I will bow; if it is an edict of the Jin state, I will not.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shijiang, deputy pacification commissioner of Chuan and Shaan, ordered Zhongzhi to bring his troops to join forces in Shaanxi. On the march at Yan'an, the rebel general Zhao Weiqing seized Zhongzhi and forced him to bow to an edict. Zhongzhi said, "If it is an edict of our dynasty, I will bow. If it is an edict of the Jin state, I will not.

sentences.zh: ”惟清械詣其右副元帥撒離曷，不能屈。

translations.literal: " Weiqing bound him in fetters and sent him to the Right Deputy Marshal Salihu, but could not break him.
translations.idiomatic: " Weiqing bound him in fetters and sent him to the Right Deputy Marshal Salihu, but could not break him.

sentences.zh: 使甲士引詣慶陽城下，諭使降，忠植大呼曰：“我河東步佛山忠義人也，為金人所執，使來招降，願將士勿負朝廷，堅守城壁。

translations.literal: Armored soldiers were sent to lead him to the foot of the Qingyang wall to urge surrender. Zhongzhi shouted loudly, "I am a loyalist of Bufoshan in Hedong. The Jurchens have seized me and sent me to invite surrender. I ask you, officers and soldiers, do not fail the court and hold firm to the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Armored soldiers were sent to lead him to the foot of the Qingyang wall to urge surrender. Zhongzhi shouted loudly, "I am a loyalist of Bufoshan in Hedong. The Jurchens have seized me and sent me to invite surrender. I ask you, officers and soldiers, do not fail the court and hold firm to the walls.

sentences.zh: 忠植即死城下。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi will die right here beneath the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi will die right here beneath the wall.

sentences.zh: ”撒離曷怒詰之，忠植披襟大呼曰：“當速殺我。

translations.literal: " Salihu questioned him in anger. Zhongzhi threw open his robe and shouted, "Kill me at once.
translations.idiomatic: " Salihu questioned him in anger. Zhongzhi threw open his robe and shouted, "Kill me at once.

sentences.zh: ”遂遇害。

translations.literal: " He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 世將上其事，贈奉國軍節度使、開府儀同三司，官其家十人。

translations.literal: Shijiang reported the matter to the throne. Zhongzhi was posthumously given the title of military commissioner of the Fengguo Army and Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and ten members of his family were given office.
translations.idiomatic: Shijiang reported the matter to the throne. Zhongzhi was posthumously given the title of military commissioner of the Fengguo Army and Grand Preceptor with honors equal to the Three Excellencies, and ten members of his family were given office.

sentences.zh: 唐琦，本衛士。

translations.literal: Tang Qi had originally been an imperial guardsman.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qi had originally been an imperial guardsman.

sentences.zh: 建炎間，高宗航海，琦病留越州。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan period, when Emperor Gaozong went to sea, Qi was ill and remained in Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan period, when Emperor Gaozong went to sea, Qi was ill and remained in Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 李鄴以城降，金人琶八守之，琦袖石伏道旁，伺其出，擊之，不中被執。

translations.literal: Li Ye surrendered the city; the Jurchen Pa Ba guarded it. Qi hid a stone in his sleeve and lay in wait by the road; when Pa Ba came out he struck at him, missed, and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye surrendered the city, and the Jurchen Pa Ba guarded it. Qi hid a stone in his sleeve and lay in wait by the road. When Pa Ba came out he struck at him, missed, and was seized.

sentences.zh: 琶八詰之，琦曰：“欲碎爾首，死為趙氏鬼耳。

translations.literal: Pa Ba questioned him. Qi said, "I wished to smash your head—I would die only to become a ghost of the Zhao house.
translations.idiomatic: Pa Ba questioned him. Qi said, "I wished to smash your head. I would die only to become a ghost of the Zhao house.

sentences.zh: ”琶八曰：“使人人如此，趙氏豈至是哉。

translations.literal: " Pa Ba said, "If everyone were like this, how could the Zhao house have come to this?
translations.idiomatic: " Pa Ba said, "If everyone were like this, how could the Zhao house have come to this?

sentences.zh: ”又問曰：“李鄴為帥尚以城降，汝何人，敢爾？

translations.literal: " He asked again, "Li Ye was commander and still surrendered the city—who are you to dare such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: " He asked again, "Li Ye was commander and still surrendered the city. Who are you to dare such a thing?

sentences.zh: ”琦曰：“鄴為臣不忠，吾恨不得手刃之，尚何言斯人為！

translations.literal: " Qi said, "Ye was disloyal as a minister—I only regret that I could not cut him down with my own hand. Why speak of such a man!
translations.idiomatic: " Qi said, "Ye was disloyal as a minister. I only regret that I could not cut him down with my own hand. Why speak of such a man!

sentences.zh: ” 乃顧鄴曰：“我月給才石五鬥米，不肯背其主，爾享國厚恩乃若此，豈復齒人類哉？

translations.literal: " He then turned to Ye and said, "My monthly pay was only five dou of rice—I would not betray my lord. You enjoyed the state's deep grace and acted thus. How can you still be counted among humankind?
translations.idiomatic: " He then turned to Ye and said, "My monthly pay was only five dou of rice, yet I would not betray my lord. You enjoyed the state's deep grace and acted thus. How can you still be counted among humankind?

sentences.zh: ”詬罵不少屈，琶八趣殺之，至死不絕口。

translations.literal: " He reviled them without yielding in the least. Pa Ba hurried to kill him, and to his death he did not cease his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: " He reviled them without yielding in the least. Pa Ba hurried to kill him, and to his death he did not cease his curses.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔為立廟，賜名旌忠。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered a temple built for him and granted the name Commending Loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported to the throne, an edict ordered a temple built for him and granted the name Commending Loyalty.

sentences.zh: 李震，汴人也。

translations.literal: Li Zhen was a man of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen was a man of Bian.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，金人迫京師，震時為小校，率所部三百人出戰，殺人馬七百餘，已而被執。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingkang, when the Jurchens pressed the capital, Zhen was then a junior officer; he led three hundred men of his command into battle and killed more than seven hundred men and horses, but was afterward seized.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jingkang, when the Jurchens pressed the capital, Zhen was a junior officer. He led three hundred men of his command into battle and killed more than seven hundred men and horses, but was afterward seized.

sentences.zh: 金人曰：“南朝皇帝安在？

translations.literal: The Jurchens said, "Where is the emperor of the Southern Court?
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens said, "Where is the emperor of the Southern Court?

sentences.zh: ”震曰：“我官家非爾所當問。

translations.literal: " Zhen said, "My sovereign is not for you to ask about.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhen said, "My sovereign is not for you to ask about.

sentences.zh: ”金人怒，絣諸庭柱，臠割之，膚肉垂盡，腹有餘氣，猶罵不絕口。

translations.literal: " The Jurchens were enraged, bound him to a courtyard pillar, and cut him to pieces; his flesh was nearly all gone, yet breath remained in his belly and he still reviled them without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jurchens were enraged, bound him to a courtyard pillar, and cut him to pieces. His flesh was nearly all gone, yet breath remained in his belly and he still reviled them without cease.

sentences.zh: 陳求道，字得之，鹹寧人。

translations.literal: Chen Qiudao, style name Dezhi, was a native of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qiudao, styled Dezhi, was a native of Xianning.

sentences.zh: 登進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the civil service examination.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the civil service examination.

sentences.zh: 靖康間判都水監。

translations.literal: During the Jingkang period he served as acting director of the Directorate of Waterways.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingkang period he served as acting director of the Directorate of Waterways.

sentences.zh: 及朝議二帝出郊請和，求道力爭之，不聽。

translations.literal: When the court debated having the two emperors go out of the city to sue for peace, Qiudao strove against it strenuously, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated having the two emperors go out of the city to sue for peace, Qiudao strove against it strenuously but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 欽宗知康王兵眾，求道請以元帥加之，齎蠟書者八人皆遇害，惟求道所薦劉定致書而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Qinzong knew that the Prince of Kang had many troops; Qiudao asked that the title of commander be added to him. Of the eight men who carried the sealed letters, all met disaster; only Liu Ding, whom Qiudao had recommended, delivered the letter and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Qinzong knew that the Prince of Kang had many troops. Qiudao asked that the title of commander be added to him. Of the eight men who carried the sealed letters, all met disaster. Only Liu Ding, whom Qiudao had recommended, delivered the letter and returned.

sentences.zh: 金人立張邦昌，下令在京官不朝者死，求道稱疾不往，嘔血累日。

translations.literal: The Jurchens enthroned Zhang Bangchang and ordered that officials in the capital who did not attend court would die. Qiudao claimed illness and did not go, vomiting blood for many days.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens enthroned Zhang Bangchang and ordered that officials in the capital who did not attend court would die. Qiudao claimed illness and did not go, vomiting blood for many days.

sentences.zh: 開封尹親以邦昌命召之，竟不能屈。

translations.literal: The Prefect of Kaifeng came in person with Bangchang's order to summon him, yet could not make him yield.
translations.idiomatic: The Prefect of Kaifeng came in person with Bangchang's order to summon him, yet could not make him yield.

sentences.zh: 求道以二帝蒙塵，屢欲自殺，因救得免。

translations.literal: Qiudao, because the two emperors were in dust and hardship, repeatedly wished to kill himself, but was saved and escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Because the two emperors were in dust and hardship, Qiudao repeatedly wished to kill himself but was saved and escaped death.

sentences.zh: 先是，陳留河決，四十餘日漕輸不通，京城大恐，開封尹宗澤命求道治之，七日河盡復故道。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Chenliu River had burst its banks; for more than forty days transport on the canal was cut off and the capital was greatly alarmed. The Prefect of Kaifeng Zong Ze ordered Qiudao to repair it, and within seven days the river entirely returned to its old course.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Chenliu River had burst its banks. For more than forty days transport on the canal was cut off and the capital was greatly alarmed. The Prefect of Kaifeng Zong Ze ordered Qiudao to repair it, and within seven days the river entirely returned to its old course.

sentences.zh: 建炎四年，命為襄、鄧、隨、郢鎮撫，以奏兵食不給，待命未行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianyan he was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Xiang, Deng, Sui, and Ying, but memorialized that troops and provisions were insufficient and awaited orders without departing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianyan he was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Xiang, Deng, Sui, and Ying, but memorialized that troops and provisions were insufficient and awaited orders without departing.

sentences.zh: 自鹹寧挈家就食嘉魚，值亂兵起，乃之蒲圻，寓龍堂僧寺。

translations.literal: He took his family from Xianning to seek food in Jiayu; when disorderly troops rose he went to Puqi and lodged at the Longtang Buddhist temple.
translations.idiomatic: He took his family from Xianning to seek food in Jiayu. When disorderly troops rose he went to Puqi and lodged at the Longtang Buddhist temple.

sentences.zh: 未久，招撫劉忠叛，一夕數千人麇至，驅求道家還嘉魚。

translations.literal: Before long the pacification officer Liu Zhong rebelled; in one night several thousand men gathered and drove Qiudao's family back to Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the pacification officer Liu Zhong rebelled. In one night several thousand men gathered and drove Qiudao's family back to Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 至茗山逆旅，具酒食奉求道為主，將南走湖湘。

translations.literal: At an inn on Mount Ming they prepared wine and food and made Qiudao their leader, intending to flee south to Hunan and Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: At an inn on Mount Ming they prepared wine and food and made Qiudao their leader, intending to flee south to Hunan and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 求道正色厲辭，賊怒，殺求道妻蔡及二子符、佺，必欲從己。

translations.literal: Qiudao spoke with stern countenance and fierce words. The rebels were enraged, killed Qiudao's wife Cai and his two sons Fu and Quan, and insisted that he follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Qiudao spoke with stern countenance and fierce words. The rebels were enraged, killed Qiudao's wife Cai and his two sons Fu and Quan, and insisted that he follow them.

sentences.zh: 求道罵愈厲，賊斫其口拔出舌斷之。

translations.literal: Qiudao reviled them ever more fiercely; the rebels hacked open his mouth, pulled out his tongue, and cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Qiudao reviled them ever more fiercely. The rebels hacked open his mouth, pulled out his tongue, and cut it off.

sentences.zh: 獨符子凱竄山谷得免。

translations.literal: Only his son Zikai fled into the mountains and valleys and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Only his son Zikai fled into the mountains and escaped.

sentences.zh: 賊退，始得求道屍，瘞於興陂。

translations.literal: When the rebels withdrew, they at last obtained Qiudao's corpse and buried it at Xingpi.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels withdrew, they at last obtained Qiudao's corpse and buried it at Xingpi.
